9:31.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابࣰ ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَسِيحَ ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ اۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
9:31.en: They have taken as lords beside Allah their rabbis and their monks and the Messiah son of Mary, when they were bidden to worship only One Allah. There is no Allah save Him. Be He Glorified from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

9:34.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡبَارِ وَٱلرُّهۡبَانِ لَيَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلۡفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
9:34.en: O ye who believe! Lo! many of the (Jewish) rabbis and the (Christian) monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar (men) from the way of Allah. They who hoard up gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah, unto them give tidings (O Muhammad) of a painful doom

9:35.ar: يَوۡمَ يُحۡمَىٰ عَلَيۡهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكۡوَىٰ بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمۡ وَجُنُوبُهُمۡ وَظُهُورُهُمۡۖ هَٰذَا مَا كَنَزۡتُمۡ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡنِزُونَ
9:35.en: On the day when it will (all) be heated in the fire of hell, and their foreheads and their flanks and their backs will be branded therewith (and it will be said unto them): Here is that which ye hoarded for yourselves. Now taste of what ye used to hoard

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

9:72.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَمَسَٰكِنَ طَيِّبَةࣰ فِي جَنَّٰتِ عَدۡنࣲۚ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:72.en: Allah promiseth to the believers, men and women, Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide - blessed dwellings in Gardens of Eden. And - greater (far)! - acceptance from Allah. That is the supreme triumph

9:84.ar: وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُم مَّاتَ أَبَدࣰ ا وَلَا تَقُمۡ عَلَىٰ قَبۡرِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
9:84.en: And never (O Muhammad) pray for one of them who dieth, nor stand by his grave. Lo! they disbelieved in Allah and His messenger, and they died while they were evil-doers

9:102.ar: وَءَاخَرُونَ ٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡ خَلَطُواْ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَءَاخَرَ سَيِّئًا عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
9:102.en: And (there are) others who have acknowledged their faults. They mixed a righteous action with another that was bad. It may be that Allah will relent toward them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

zpe5IJ1XeMY.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 10: Quranic Reflections (At-Tawbah)
zpe5IJ1XeMY.one_line: At-Tawbah on the ummah's relationships: scholars neither idolised nor dismissed, the cave and sadness, Allah's pleasure, Ibn Ubayy's funeral, honest repentance, and the sale to Allah.
zpe5IJ1XeMY.summary: Marking a third of Ramadan as a checkpoint, he introduces at-Tawbah as the surah defining the ummah's relationships, which he considers vital for Muslims in Canada. The first is with scholars: earlier communities raised their clergy to near-divine status, who then exploited people's wealth. Muslims swing between treating scholars as infallible and dismissing the whole structure of knowledge; scholars are human and their work must be tested by evidence, and sacred knowledge must never be sold, as his own Quran teacher showed by refusing a gift. In the cave during the hijrah, after every precaution, the Prophet told Abu Bakr not to grieve: fear is natural, but sadness at an unfinished mission is avoided by having done everything possible. Allah's pleasure is greater than all of Paradise, as the Prophet's prayer at Ta'if shows. The Prophet prayed over Abdullah ibn Ubayy out of compassion before the ruling forbade it, showing love behind the law. Those who admit their sins without excuses are the model for repentance, and Allah's purchase of believers' lives and wealth for Paradise shows how highly He values each person, as the Ansar understood at their pledge.

outline.heading: The tenth night as a checkpoint
outline.gist: A third of the month is done: evaluate what you hoped to achieve and how far you still need to go.

outline.heading: Ramadan in thirds: mercy, forgiveness, freedom
outline.gist: The report dividing Ramadan into thirds has weak authenticity, but scholars long accepted the idea, so tonight is the last night of mercy.

outline.heading: At-Tawbah: the ummah's relationships
outline.gist: The only surah without the basmalah because of its stern opening; it defines relations with every group inside and outside the ummah, which matters greatly for Muslims in Canada.

outline.heading: A healthy relationship with scholars
outline.gist: Other communities placed clergy between human and divine; in Islam scholars and preachers are people held to the same standard, and excess power corrupts them and the deen.

outline.heading: Clergy who devour people's wealth
outline.gist: Many rabbis and monks misused people's money; the hoarded gold will be heated and pressed on their foreheads, sides and backs.

outline.heading: Two extremes: infallible scholars or none at all
outline.gist: The verse is for us: some Muslims treat scholars' words as sacred and beyond critique, others reject the whole structure of Islamic knowledge; both are unacceptable.

outline.heading: Scholars are human: weigh their work by evidence
outline.gist: Their intellectual output must be examined by evidence and reason without diminishing their status, and knowledge must never become a commodity.

outline.heading: The teacher who refused a gift
outline.gist: When his father offered money after he completed his Quran recitation, the sheikh was deeply offended and nearly withdrew the ijazah.

outline.heading: Sacred knowledge has no price
outline.gist: No sum could compensate for the Quran and Sunnah; both learner and teacher must honour it, because a scholar who degrades himself degrades the knowledge he carries.

outline.heading: Do not grieve, Allah is with us
outline.gist: Driven from his home, the Prophet in the cave told his companion not to grieve; Allah sent tranquility and unseen soldiers.

outline.heading: Every precaution for the hijrah
outline.gist: He slept outside for a month to normalise it, left at noon, hid three nights in a cave in the opposite direction, had a shepherd cover their tracks and walked without camels.

outline.heading: The pursuers at the mouth of the cave
outline.gist: Despite everything they reached the exact cave; Abu Bakr said if one looked down at his feet he would see them.

outline.heading: Not fear but sadness
outline.gist: Fear was natural and not forbidden; Abu Bakr's grief was that the mission might end before Medina, and the Prophet reminded him they had done all they could.

outline.heading: They simply did not look
outline.gist: No one glanced at the small opening, perhaps Allah's unseen soldiers working in their minds; the pursuers learned only later how close they had been.

outline.heading: Courage, and no regrets at the end
outline.gist: The scene teaches bravery and that what we must avoid at life's end is sadness over not having given our lives to Allah.

outline.heading: Allah's good pleasure is greater
outline.gist: Amid gardens and every pleasure, the most valuable thing in Paradise is knowing Allah is fully pleased with you.

outline.heading: Ta'if: as long as You are not displeased with me
outline.gist: Stoned and stranded, bleeding, the Prophet prayed that he could bear anything provided it was not a sign of Allah's anger; a true Muslim keeps asking whether he pleases Allah.

outline.heading: Never displeased with you again
outline.gist: In Paradise Allah declares lasting pleasure with its people, which comforts them more than what no eye has seen.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the worst of enemies
outline.gist: Claiming Islam, he spread rumours about the Prophet's wife, sabotaged him at Uhud and insulted the companions, while his son was a great companion.

outline.heading: The son's request and the funeral prayer
outline.gist: When the tearful son asked, the Prophet could not refuse and prayed over him while Umar protested; the Prophet knew who the hypocrites were, whereas we can only guess.

outline.heading: In death the rivalries end
outline.gist: Death shows there is no real winning or losing; understanding it makes you pity even the worst person, now utterly powerless.

outline.heading: Revealed afterwards, by design
outline.gist: The prohibition came after the prayer so we would see that the Prophet's attitude was compassion and love, with rulings still to be followed.

outline.heading: The verse scholars claimed for themselves
outline.gist: Over a hundred scholars said this verse described them best: those in the middle who admit their sins openly, mixing good and bad deeds.

outline.heading: Come clean, with no excuses
outline.gist: Do not rationalise or offer half apologies; say you were wrong, ask forgiveness and ask Him to make you better.

outline.heading: Allah has purchased your self and your wealth
outline.gist: Your life, choices and possessions in exchange for Paradise; no one fulfils covenants like Allah, so be optimistic about the deal.

outline.heading: The price tag is you
outline.gist: He judged you worth Paradise, so no one can say you lack value; the question is whether you will hand yourself over.

outline.heading: The pledge of the Ansar: nothing but Paradise
outline.gist: At the pledge with the people of Yathrib the Prophet listed their obligations and promised only Paradise; they kept their side to the end.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The tenth night is a checkpoint and the close of the third devoted to mercy.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Scholars are human and their work must be tested by evidence; knowledge must never be priced or sold.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Avoid both idolising scholars and rejecting Islamic scholarship altogether.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: The Prophet took every precaution and then relied on Allah, who protected them in the cave.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Fear is natural; courage is acting through it, and the regret to avoid is not having given one's all.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Allah's pleasure is the greatest reward, and a true believer's constant concern is not to displease Him.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Ibn Ubayy harmed the Prophet more than any open enemy while claiming Islam.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: The Prophet's compassion extended even to his worst enemy at death.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death shows that worldly competition was never real winning or losing.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Repentance means admitting wrong without excuses and asking to be made better.

themes.label: Self-value, self-worth, confidence
themes.note: Allah valued each believer at the price of Paradise.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: The covenant with Allah exchanges self and wealth for Paradise; Allah fulfils it, and the Ansar fulfilled theirs.

hadith.gist: Ramadan is divided into thirds: the first mercy, the middle forgiveness and the last freedom from the fire; he notes the chain is weak.
At Ta'if the Prophet prayed that as long as Allah was not angry with him, he did not mind what befell him.
Allah tells the people of Paradise that He is pleased with them and will never be displeased with them again.
Paradise holds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined.
The Prophet prayed the funeral prayer for Abdullah ibn Ubayy at his son's request despite Umar's objection, and then the prohibition was revealed.
At the pledge with the people of Yathrib, the Prophet promised them Paradise and nothing else in return for their commitments.

maxims: Scholars are people, held to the same standard
Sacred knowledge has no price tag
Fear is natural; the regret to avoid is sadness
There is no real winning or losing; we all die
Come clean with Allah, no half apologies
The price tag is you

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

23:31.ar: ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ قَرۡنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
23:31.en: Then, after them, We brought forth another generation

23:32.ar: فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا فِيهِمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥٓۚ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
23:32.en: And we sent among them a messenger of their own, saying: Serve Allah, Ye have no other Allah save Him. Will ye not ward off (evil)

23:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِن قَوۡمِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِلِقَآءِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَأَتۡرَفۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يَأۡكُلُ مِمَّا تَأۡكُلُونَ مِنۡهُ وَيَشۡرَبُ مِمَّا تَشۡرَبُونَ
23:33.en: And the chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had made soft in the life of the world, said: This is only a mortal like you, who eateth of that whereof ye eat and drinketh of that ye drink

23:34.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَطَعۡتُم بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَكُمۡ إِنَّكُمۡ إِذࣰ ا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
23:34.en: If ye were to obey a mortal like yourselves, then, lo! ye surely would be losers

23:35.ar: أَيَعِدُكُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ إِذَا مِتُّمۡ وَكُنتُمۡ تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخۡرَجُونَ
23:35.en: Doth he promise you that you, when ye are dead and have become dust and bones, will (again) be brought forth

23:36.en: Begone, begone, with that which ye are promised

23:37.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنۡيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحۡيَا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَبۡعُوثِينَ
23:37.en: There is naught but our life of the world; we die and we live, and we shall not be raised (again)

23:38.ar: إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا وَمَا نَحۡنُ لَهُۥ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
23:38.en: He is only a man who hath invented a lie about Allah. We are not going to put faith in him

23:39.en: He said: My Lord! Help me because they deny me

23:40.en: He said: In a little while they surely will become repentant

23:41.ar: فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ غُثَآءࣰۚ فَبُعۡدࣰ ا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
23:41.en: So the (Awful) Cry overtook them rightfully, and We made them like as wreckage (that a torrent hurleth). A far removal for wrongdoing folk

23:112.ar: قَٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
23:112.en: He will say: How long tarried ye in the earth, counting by years

23:113.ar: قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ
23:113.en: They will say: We tarried by a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count

23:114.ar: قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
23:114.en: He will say: Ye tarried but a little if ye only knew

24:2.ar: ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجۡلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا مِاْئَةَ جَلۡدَةࣲۖ وَلَا تَأۡخُذۡكُم بِهِمَا رَأۡفَةࣱ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۖ وَلۡيَشۡهَدۡ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
24:2.en: The adulterer and the adulteress, scourge ye each one of them (with) a hundred stripes. And let not pity for the twain withhold you from obedience to Allah, if ye believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a party of believers witness their punishment

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

24:12.ar: لَّوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ بِأَنفُسِهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا وَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِفۡكࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
24:12.en: Why did not the believers, men and women, when ye heard it, think good of their own own folk, and say: It is a manifest untruth

24:13.ar: لَّوۡلَا جَآءُو عَلَيۡهِ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَۚ فَإِذۡ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِٱلشُّهَدَآءِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
24:13.en: Why did they not produce four witnesses? Since they produce not witnesses, they verily are liars in the sight of Allah

24:14.ar: وَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَتُهُۥ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكُمۡ فِي مَآ أَفَضۡتُمۡ فِيهِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
24:14.en: Had it not been for the grace of Allah and His mercy unto you in the world and the Hereafter an awful doom had overtaken you for that whereof ye murmured

24:15.ar: إِذۡ تَلَقَّوۡنَهُۥ بِأَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ وَتَحۡسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنࣰ ا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:15.en: When ye welcomed it with your tongues, and uttered with your mouths that whereof ye had no knowledge, ye counted it a trifle. In the sight of Allah it is very great

24:16.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهۡتَٰنٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:16.en: Wherefor, when ye heard it, said ye not: It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to Thee (O Allah)! This is awful calumny

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

80:2.en: Because the blind man came unto him

80:3.en: What could inform thee but that he might grow (in grace)

80:4.en: Or take heed and so the reminder might avail him

80:5.en: As for him who thinketh himself independent

80:7.en: Yet it is not thy concern if he grow not (in grace)

80:8.en: But as for him who cometh unto thee with earnest purpose

20:103.ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا عَشۡرࣰ ا
20:103.en: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days)

20:104.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذۡ يَقُولُ أَمۡثَلُهُمۡ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا يَوۡمࣰ ا
20:104.en: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day

W1H7tPwSWFQ.speaker: adnan
W1H7tPwSWFQ.speaker_note: leads the nightly Ramadan reflections in London and speaks of his own daily conversations with community members
W1H7tPwSWFQ.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 17: Quranic Reflections (Al-Hajj, Al-Mu'minun, An-Nur)
W1H7tPwSWFQ.one_line: Striving without limit, investing in people over audiences, the shortness of life, rejecting slander through good assumptions, and lowering the gaze.
W1H7tPwSWFQ.summary: Continuing the cluster on carrying the message, he closes al-Hajj with its final verse: strive for Allah without limit, know that the deen holds no hardship even if the childish nafs feels every rule as a restriction, take the Prophet as the standard, and hold fast to Allah. Al-Mu'minun teaches that the value lies in people, so he argues against chasing views and reach and for investing in those in front of you locally. Its unnamed prophet stands for every prophet rejected by elites made arrogant and materialistic by excess wealth. The question of how long people stayed on earth shows how short life will seem, and the regret of those who kept saying they had time. An-Nur shows how a society keeps its light: through ethics. From the slander against Aisha he teaches that what you assume about others reflects yourself, that hearsay must be rejected even without certainty, and that Muslims want faults covered, not exposed. He ends with lowering the gaze, which comes before any talk of hijab, and asks the community to honour sisters who carry the visible weight of Islam.

outline.heading: Opening
Carrying the message is a journey
outline.gist: Carrying the message means living Islam, guarding it and taking it to others; al-Hajj, named after a pilgrimage, frames this as a journey with ups and downs.

outline.heading: Strive for Allah as He deserves
outline.gist: The command sets no ceiling on striving: identify difficulties, push against them and keep moving, because He chose you for this.

outline.heading: No hardship in the deen: the nafs is still a child
outline.gist: A rule only feels like a restriction to a nafs that wants everything at all times, like a child; the intellect should see past that perception.

outline.heading: The way of Ibrahim and the Prophet as the standard
outline.gist: Measure yourself against how the Prophet thought, spoke and behaved; living up to that example makes you an example for others.

outline.heading: Prayer and zakat as symbols of two kinds of worship
outline.gist: Prayer stands for worship between you and Allah, zakat for worship that serves others; together they sum up all the rulings.

outline.heading: Hold fast to Allah, the best protector
outline.gist: He walks through the verse as one journey and calls it one of the most beautiful endings of any surah.

outline.heading: Al-Mu'minun: the value is in people
outline.gist: He maps the cluster: family in Maryam, fulfilment in Ta-Ha, role models in al-Anbiya, the journey in al-Hajj, and people as the true value in al-Mu'minun.

outline.heading: Quality over quantity: views mean nothing
outline.gist: Buildings, logos and online reach do not matter; a million views change no one, and the Prophet reached millions by investing in individuals.

outline.heading: Serve the people where Allah placed you
outline.gist: Beyond emergency aid abroad, build the people around you here in London, just as the Prophet was told to focus on the person in front of him.

outline.heading: One unnamed prophet for every prophet
outline.gist: Scholars proposed every possible prophet, which suggests a generic story: the elite who denied resurrection had been given more than they needed.

outline.heading: Excess wealth changes attitude
outline.gist: People with more than they need grow arrogant and stop taking things seriously; we speak rightly only when we sense our need.

outline.heading: A man who eats and drinks like you
outline.gist: Seeing through a materialist lens, they dismissed their prophet as an ordinary man and mocked the promise of resurrection.

outline.heading: Possessed by possessions
outline.gist: Luxury and indulgence lead people to value only what can be counted and to raise children that way; soon they regret it.

outline.heading: How long did you remain on earth?
outline.gist: After thousands of years standing on that Day, seventy years on earth barely register in memory; the question is sincere, not mockery.

outline.heading: Ask those who keep count
outline.gist: Like misjudging how long one spent abroad decades ago, they guess a day or part of a day and defer to whoever kept count.

outline.heading: If only you had known: the illusion of 'I have time'
outline.gist: Their number is wrong but their sense is right: life was short, yet back then people kept postponing learning, prayer and change until later.

outline.heading: Right in concept, wrong in number: the pain of regret
outline.gist: Even the largest guess of ten days is correct in essence; the verse carries the regret of hearts that wasted a short time.

outline.heading: An-Nur: light that protects society
outline.gist: The surah opens with the ruling on public fornication because a society that normalises the haram loses its light.

outline.heading: The incident of the slander against Aisha
outline.gist: Left behind by the army, she was brought back by Safwan and fell ill, while the hypocrites' circle spread rumours about them.

outline.heading: No message without ethics
outline.gist: A person involved in riba or talebearing carries a darkened message that goes nowhere; certain behaviours must go first.

outline.heading: Slander as the gravest of these behaviours
outline.gist: Some good Muslims repeated the rumour, but once the verses came they held their tongues and never did it again.

outline.heading: Good assumptions of yourselves
outline.gist: The believers should have thought well of themselves: what you assume of others mirrors what you would have done in their place.

outline.heading: What people say about you reflects them
outline.gist: Most people are not thinking about you; when they do speak ill, it reveals how they see themselves and the world, so it is not personal.

outline.heading: Reject hearsay even without certainty
outline.gist: They could not swear it was false, yet the duty was to deny it anyway: unwitnessed and unproven means it did not happen.

outline.heading: Abu Ayyub and his wife: simple logic against rumour
outline.gist: Asked whether she would have done such a thing, each answered no, and concluded that Aisha and Safwan, better than them, would not either.

outline.heading: Muslims crave covering faults
outline.gist: A believer does not want a sin proven or exposed; we live for covering people's mistakes and not normalising the haram.

outline.heading: You thought it trivial, but it is grave with Allah
outline.gist: Idle talk about someone's honour inflicts almost indescribable pain; treat others as you would want to be treated if you were the target.

outline.heading: Tell the believers: lowering the gaze as a sign of belief
outline.gist: Grammatically the verse says that once told, true believers will lower their gaze and guard their chastity; Allah knows what they imagine.

outline.heading: The added command for women
outline.gist: Women also lower the gaze and guard chastity, and additionally cover hair, neck and chest except before close male relatives.

outline.heading: Men first: before judging hijab, lower your gaze
outline.gist: Men who get upset about hijab should first account for how much they lower their gaze, on the street and on the phone in their hand.

outline.heading: Hijab is linguistically clear and the gaze is no joke
outline.gist: The Arabic allows no other reading of the covering; young men laugh when told to lower their gaze, but the verse ties it to true belief.

outline.heading: Every extra command brings extra reward
outline.gist: Women's test in this area is harder, so their reward for chastity is greater than men's.

outline.heading: The deen does not change, and no one is looked down on
outline.gist: Islam is not adjusted to taste, but a sister who struggles with hijab must not be judged or mistreated; pray for her strength.

outline.heading: Sisters in hijab are the front line
outline.gist: Men can blend in, but women who wear hijab carry Islam visibly in countries where Muslims are minorities, and that must be acknowledged.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: There is no limit to striving for Allah, and the deen itself is not a hardship though the nafs perceives rules as restrictions.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip

20:2.en: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day

21:1.ar: ٱقۡتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ فِي غَفۡلَةࣲ مُّعۡرِضُونَ
21:1.en: Their reckoning draweth nigh for mankind, while they turn away in heedlessness

21:2.ar: مَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن ذِكۡرࣲ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحۡدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسۡتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمۡ يَلۡعَبُونَ
21:2.en: Never cometh there unto them a new reminder from their Lord but they listen to it while they play

21:3.ar: لَاهِيَةࣰ قُلُوبُهُمۡۗ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجۡوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ هَلۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُكُمۡۖ أَفَتَأۡتُونَ ٱلسِّحۡرَ وَأَنتُمۡ تُبۡصِرُونَ
21:3.en: With hearts preoccupied. And they confer in secret. The wrong-doers say: Is this other than a mortal like you? Will ye then succumb to magic when ye see (it)

21:47.ar: وَنَضَعُ ٱلۡمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلۡقِسۡطَ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةࣲ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلٍ أَتَيۡنَا بِهَاۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
21:47.en: And We set a just balance for the Day of Resurrection so that no soul is wronged in aught. Though it be of the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We bring it. And We suffice for reckoners

21:51.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ رُشۡدَهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
21:51.en: And We verily gave Abraham of old his proper course, and We were Aware of him

21:52.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
21:52.en: When he said unto his father and his folk: What are these images unto which ye pay devotion

21:53.en: They said: We found our fathers worshippers of them

21:54.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُمۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
21:54.en: He said: Verily ye and your fathers were in plain error

21:55.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ أَمۡ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
21:55.en: They said: Bringest thou unto us the truth, or art thou some jester

21:56.ar: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمۡ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
21:56.en: He said: Nay, but your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them; and I am of those who testify unto that

21:57.ar: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَٰمَكُم بَعۡدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
21:57.en: And, by Allah, I shall circumvent your idols after ye have gone away and turned your backs

21:58.ar: فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ يَرۡجِعُونَ
21:58.en: Then he reduced them to fragments, all save the chief of them, that haply they might have recourse to it

21:59.ar: قَالُواْ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:59.en: They said: Who hath done this to our gods? Surely it must be some evil-doer

21:60.ar: قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا فَتࣰ ى يَذۡكُرُهُمۡ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:60.en: They said: We heard a youth make mention of them, who is called Abraham

21:61.ar: قَالُواْ فَأۡتُواْ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡهَدُونَ
21:61.en: They said: Then bring him (hither) before the people's eyes that they may testify

21:62.ar: قَالُوٓاْ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلۡتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:62.en: They said: Is it thou who hast done this to our gods, O Abraham

21:63.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمۡ هَٰذَا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُمۡ إِن كَانُواْ يَنطِقُونَ
21:63.en: He said: But this, their chief hath done it. So question them, if they can speak

21:64.ar: فَرَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
21:64.en: Then gathered they apart and said: Lo! ye yourselves are the wrong-doers

21:65.ar: ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
21:65.en: And they were utterly confounded, and they said: Well thou knowest that these speak not

21:66.ar: قَالَ أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ
21:66.en: He said: Worship ye then instead of Allah that which cannot profit you at all, nor harm you

21:67.ar: أُفࣲّ لَّكُمۡ وَلِمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
21:67.en: Fie on you and all that ye worship instead of Allah! Have ye then no sense

21:68.ar: قَالُواْ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓاْ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ فَٰعِلِينَ
21:68.en: They cried: Burn him and stand by your gods, if ye will be doing

21:69.ar: قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ
21:69.en: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham

21:70.ar: وَأَرَادُواْ بِهِۦ كَيۡدࣰ ا فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡأَخۡسَرِينَ
21:70.en: And they wished to set a snare for him, but We made them the greater losers

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And among mankind is he who worshippeth Allah upon a narrow marge so that if good befalleth him he is content therewith, but if a trial befalleth him, he falleth away utterly. He loseth both the world and the Hereafter. That is the sheer loss

22:46.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ يَعۡقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ ءَاذَانࣱ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
22:46.en: Have they not travelled in the land, and have they hearts wherewith to feel and ears wherewith to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts, which are within the bosoms, that grow blind

3:173.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ قَدۡ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمۡ فَٱخۡشَوۡهُمۡ فَزَادَهُمۡ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَقَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡوَكِيلُ
3:173.en: Those unto whom men said: Lo! the people have gathered against you, therefor fear them. (The threat of danger) but increased the faith of them and they cried: Allah is Sufficient for us! Most Excellent is He in Whom we trust

17:81.ar: وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقࣰ ا
17:81.en: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish

cYj3KlANcCI.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 16: Quranic Reflections (Ta-Ha, Al-Anbiya, Al-Hajj)
cYj3KlANcCI.one_line: On carrying the message: turning from Allah's reminder, heedlessness, the scales of justice, Ibrahim and the idols, faith on an edge, and blind hearts.
cYj3KlANcCI.summary: He presents Ta-Ha, al-Anbiya and al-Hajj as a cluster on carrying the message: it is meant to bring fulfilment, its role models are the prophets, and it is a journey needing flexibility, perseverance and striving. From Ta-Ha he argues that the deen reminds people of what they already know innately, so turning away produces inner misery and blindness in the next life; if faith brings no peace, something is wrong. Al-Anbiya opens with people heedless as their reckoning nears, and he treats indifference as worse than hostility. The scales of justice weigh even a mustard seed, but hollow deeds eaten by showing off weigh nothing, while one sincere declaration of tawhid outweighs ninety-nine records of sin. Ibrahim's story shows a young man who valued critical thinking and a people who, faced with cognitive dissonance, doubled down and tried to burn him. Smashing the idols did not change minds, so the Prophet worked on mentalities and the idols later fell on their own. From al-Hajj he warns against worship conditional on comfort and calls for hearts that draw lessons from what they see.

outline.heading: Opening
A cluster on carrying the message
outline.gist: Ta-Ha: the message brings fulfilment not misery; al-Anbiya: the prophets are your role models; al-Hajj, revealed partly on a journey: flexibility, perseverance and striving.

outline.heading: Turning from the reminder brings a constricted life
outline.gist: The deen reminds us of a purpose we know innately; dhank is an inner state of misery and emptiness, whatever a person's outward circumstances.

outline.heading: Raised blind for forgetting what you knew
outline.gist: The one who turned away truly forgot the inner voice that knows why he is here, so he is left without sight on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: If your faith gives you no peace, something is missing
outline.gist: Commitment to the deen should grant inner peace; misery belongs to those who turn away from it.

outline.heading: The prophets as role models
outline.gist: Having people to look up to is healthy as long as they are not worshipped; al-Anbiya offers the prophets for that role.

outline.heading: The reckoning draws near while people are heedless
outline.gist: A surah that opens with no introduction: judgment rushes toward people while they drift in oblivion and turn away.

outline.heading: Indifference: the opposite of love is not hate
outline.gist: Ghaflah, spread across the whole Quran, is the state of being neither committed nor opposed; hate is still a form of passion, while indifference cannot even judge.

outline.heading: Hearts fully distracted
outline.gist: Their attention is turned elsewhere; other concerns occupy their hearts as the warning arrives.

outline.heading: Scales of justice that miss nothing
outline.gist: Even a deed the weight of a mustard seed is brought; no soul is wronged and every detail of a lifetime is weighed.

outline.heading: Hollow deeds that carry no weight
outline.gist: Deeds eaten from inside by showing off are like empty shells that leave the scale unmoved; just make sure you have something real to put in it.

outline.heading: The card that outweighed ninety-nine records
outline.gist: A man with vast records of sin is not wronged: his single card bearing the testimony of tawhid sends the records flying.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the young questioner
outline.gist: As a teenager he kept asking about idol worship and refused answers that made no sense; he valued critical thinking.

outline.heading: Breaking the idols and the big one with the axe
outline.gist: He smashed the idols while the people were at their festival; they then chose to switch off their logic on this one matter alone.

outline.heading: Cognitive dissonance and its three responses
outline.gist: Faced with a challenging fact you accept the truth, reconcile the two, or ignore it and overcommit to the false belief; a true Muslim accepts the truth.

outline.heading: Turned upside down: refusing logic
outline.gist: The phrase pictures people thinking with the wrong end; they rebuked Ibrahim for bringing reason to something they knew was false.

outline.heading: Overcompensating with a vast fire
outline.gist: Feeling weak, they built a fire so huge that he had to be catapulted into it, a show to make their stand seem worth it.

outline.heading: Allah is sufficient for me
outline.gist: In a report of weaker authenticity, Jibril offers help mid-air and Ibrahim says Allah is enough, the same words the believers later said.

outline.heading: O fire, be coolness and peace
outline.gist: Only Allah commands the elements; Ibrahim later called his days in the fire the best of his life, yet his people still did not believe.

outline.heading: Did Ibrahim's tactic work?
outline.gist: Shocking people too quickly makes them dig in and grow self-righteous; Ibrahim moved to discussion and argument instead.

outline.heading: Change the mentality and the idols fall
outline.gist: The Prophet never broke the idols around the Kaaba until the conquest, when he only pointed and they fell; go after root causes, not symptoms.

outline.heading: Worshipping Allah on an edge
outline.gist: Faith that holds only while things go well collapses at the first difficulty, losing both this world and the next.

outline.heading: Thank Allah he has not pushed you to the edge
outline.gist: Allah knows what would tip any of us over; be grateful for His protection, and treat faith as a journey with ease and hardship, not a fixed status.

outline.heading: Travel the earth with hearts that understand
outline.gist: Walk the earth, absorb your surroundings and listen to the stories of past peoples; that is how conviction forms.

outline.heading: Blind hearts, not blind eyes
outline.gist: The real loss is insight, not sight; a pandemic can kill millions and people still draw no lesson from it.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: The deen is a reminder of what the soul already knows; turning away brings inner misery, and real practice should bring peace.

themes.label: Indifference and apathy as a social disease
themes.note: Heedlessness is worse than hostility because the indifferent cannot even judge right from wrong.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The scales of justice are thorough to the smallest deed; the Day is for weighing, so bring deeds with substance.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Deeds hollowed out by showing off look like worship but weigh nothing.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Nothing is heavier than the name of Allah; one sincere testimony outweighs a lifetime of recorded sin.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim's confrontation with idol worship, the fire, and the lessons of his approach.

themes.label: Conspiracy thinking and critical thinking
themes.note: Ibrahim modelled questioning; his people show how cognitive dissonance leads groups to suspend logic and double down.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Allah is sufficient: Ibrahim's reliance as he was thrown into the fire, which Allah made cool and safe.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Shock tactics harden people; change minds through discussion and address the mindset behind false beliefs.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Faith that depends on circumstances is fragile; it is a journey requiring flexibility, perseverance and gratitude.

themes.label: Insight and drawing lessons (ibrah)
themes.note: Travel, observe and listen to history; hearts that lose insight learn nothing even from a global catastrophe.

96xUwd6eEqE.speaker: adnan
96xUwd6eEqE.speaker_note: single speaker continuing his Ramadan morning series on the Prophet's attributes
96xUwd6eEqE.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Treated His Companions
96xUwd6eEqE.one_line: The Prophet's greatest legacy was the people he invested in: educating, correcting, empowering and caring for his companions, a model of mentorship Muslims now neglect.
96xUwd6eEqE.summary: He calls this the broadest topic of the series and frames it around one idea: the Prophet left behind people, not buildings, and Islam spread because each generation invested in the next, as the great scholars did through their students. He illustrates with stories: playful affection for the bedouin Zahir, gentle correction of Khawwat, turning al-Fadl's gaze, teaching Mu'adh and Ibn Abbas personally, lifting Jabir out of a dark period through the camel sale, burying the poor convert Dhul-Bijadayn with his own hands. He shows the Prophet preparing others to lead, giving the seventeen-year-old Usamah command of an army, correcting Abu Dharr and Usamah firmly, praising Ibn Umar in a way that changed his habits, visiting the weak and the sick, spacing out reminders to avoid boredom, letting Umm Haram dream of sailing for Allah's cause, and teaching a new Muslim who spoke in prayer without harshness. The Ansar's grievance after Hunayn shows his sensitivity to people's feelings. He ends by urging mentorship: young Muslims should have many mentors to choose from, and everyone should see themselves as both mentee and mentor in a chain reaching back to the Prophet.

outline.heading: Framing: how he treated his companions
outline.gist: The broadest category in the series, since nearly all seerah and hadith involve it.

outline.heading: He invested in people
outline.gist: He acknowledged, educated, corrected and developed his companions; they were his legacy rather than towers or castles.

outline.heading: Islam spread through students
outline.gist: Scholars spread knowledge through the students they trained; achievements in science mean nothing to a society without values and direction.

outline.heading: Zahir hugged in the market
outline.gist: The Prophet playfully embraced an unattractive bedouin and told him he was precious in Allah's sight.

outline.heading: Khawwat and the gentle correction
outline.gist: A new Muslim caught sitting with women by a fire was later teased kindly about his camel until he reformed.

outline.heading: Turning al-Fadl's face at Hajj
outline.gist: When the young al-Fadl stared at a woman asking a question, the Prophet quietly turned his face away.

outline.heading: Mu'adh riding behind him
outline.gist: He used rides to teach Mu'adh and told him that he loved him.

outline.heading: A hundred verses of poetry
outline.gist: He asked a companion to recite poetry again and again, appreciating eloquence.

outline.heading: Mu'adh sent to Yemen
outline.gist: He instructed Mu'adh on the way, hinted he would not see him again, and told him despair is from Shaytan.

outline.heading: Raising the young Ibn Abbas
outline.gist: He taught Ibn Abbas to understand and live the hadith and treated him like a man, serving him water first.

outline.heading: Jabir's camel and a dark season
outline.gist: Seeing Jabir downcast, the Prophet blessed his slow camel, bargained playfully for it, then paid him and returned the camel, lifting his spirits.

outline.heading: Dhul-Bijadayn buried by his hand
outline.gist: A poor, unknown convert was buried at night by the Prophet himself with dua, so that Ibn Mas'ud wished he were in his place.

outline.heading: Preparing others to lead
outline.gist: He sent battles without himself so companions would learn to carry the message; a leader who trains no one leaves collapse behind.

outline.heading: Usamah leads an army at seventeen
outline.gist: He placed Usamah over senior companions, and Abu Bakr refused to undo the banner the Prophet had raised.

outline.heading: Pointing out mistakes firmly
outline.gist: He corrected Abu Dharr for insulting Bilal and Usamah for interceding to drop a punishment.

outline.heading: Praise that changed Ibn Umar
outline.gist: Saying Abdullah would be excellent if he prayed at night made Ibn Umar pray at night for decades.

outline.heading: Visiting the weak and the sick
outline.gist: Despite his schedule he visited the poor and sick, attended funerals, and greeted and prayed for children.

outline.heading: Reminders spaced to avoid boredom
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud held emotional reminders only on certain days, following the Prophet's practice.

outline.heading: Umm Haram dreams of the sea
outline.gist: He prayed she be among the first to sail for Allah's cause rather than dismissing her; true leadership lets people dream big.

outline.heading: The man who spoke in prayer
outline.gist: A new Muslim who answered a sneeze in salah was taught without scolding, and said he never saw a better teacher.

outline.heading: The Ansar's grievance after Hunayn
outline.gist: When the spoils went to new Muslims, the Ansar felt overlooked and the Prophet heard of it.

outline.heading: His address to the Ansar
outline.gist: He reminded them of guidance and unity, voiced their own case for them, and asked if they were not content to take the Messenger home.

outline.heading: The Ansar are my inner garment
outline.gist: He declared his closeness to them and prayed for them and generations of their descendants.

outline.heading: Sensitivity as leadership
outline.gist: Listening to people's pain, empowering and correcting them is why they loved him and carried Islam forward.

outline.heading: Young Muslims need many mentors
outline.gist: Mentorship is the missing piece; youth should have an abundance of mentors to choose from, not one or two overburdened people.

outline.heading: A chain of mentorship
outline.gist: From Jibril to the Prophet onward, each learned and then taught; everyone should be both mentee and mentor.

41:15.ar: فَأَمَّا عَادࣱ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَقَالُواْ مَنۡ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةًۖ أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُمۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةࣰۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يَجۡحَدُونَ
41:15.en: As for A'ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said: Who is mightier than us in power? Could they not see that Allah Who created them, He was mightier than them in power? And they denied Our revelations

41:16.ar: فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا صَرۡصَرࣰ ا فِيٓ أَيَّامࣲ نَّحِسَاتࣲ لِّنُذِيقَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡيِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَخۡزَىٰۖ وَهُمۡ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
41:16.en: Therefor We let loose on them a raging wind in evil days, that We might make them taste the torment of disgrace in the life of the world. And verily the doom of the Hereafter will be more shameful, and they will not be helped

41:17.ar: وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَٱسۡتَحَبُّواْ ٱلۡعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمۡ صَٰعِقَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡهُونِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
41:17.en: And as for Thamud, We gave them guidance, but they preferred blindness to the guidance, so the bolt of the doom of humiliation overtook them because of what they used to earn

41:18.en: And We delivered those who believed and used to keep their duty to Allah

41:19.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُحۡشَرُ أَعۡدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ
41:19.en: And (make mention of) the day when the enemies of Allah are gathered unto the Fire, they are driven on

41:20.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:20.en: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

41:22.ar: وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
41:22.en: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did

41:14.ar: إِذۡ جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلرُّسُلُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ قَالُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّنَا لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةࣰ فَإِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
41:14.en: When their messengers came unto them from before them and behind them, saying: Worship none but Allah! they said: If our Lord had willed, He surely would have sent down angels (unto us), so lo! we are disbelievers in that wherewith ye have been sent

4:164.ar: وَرُسُلࣰ ا قَدۡ قَصَصۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَيۡكَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَرُسُلࣰ ا لَّمۡ نَقۡصُصۡهُمۡ عَلَيۡكَۚ وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكۡلِيمࣰ ا
4:164.en: And messengers We have mentioned unto thee before and messengers We have not mentioned unto thee; and Allah spake directly unto Moses

35:24.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ اۚ وَإِن مِّنۡ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيهَا نَذِيرࣱ‏
35:24.en: Lo! We have sent thee with the Truth, a bearer of glad tidings and a warner; and there is not a nation but a warner hath passed among them

69:7.en: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees

4:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا سَوۡفَ نُصۡلِيهِمۡ نَارࣰ ا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتۡ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ جُلُودًا غَيۡرَهَا لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:56.en: Lo! Those who disbelieve Our revelations, We shall expose them to the Fire. As often as their skins are consumed We shall exchange them for fresh skins that they may taste the torment. Lo! Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

9_V5WAeFZUk.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 3 (41:15-22)
9_V5WAeFZUk.one_line: The listener's duty in dawah, the fates of 'Ad and Thamud, taqwa as long-term protection, and one's own senses testifying on the Day.
9_V5WAeFZUk.summary: He returns to the surah's theme and stresses that dawah has two sides: the one calling must be clear and must practise what he says, because 'do as I do' persuades more than words, and the one listening is accountable for actually listening rather than waiting to repeat his own line. The verses then give examples of people who refused to listen. 'Ad were mighty and arrogant, asking who was stronger than them, and were destroyed by a roaring wind; he notes that Hud and Salih were prophets to the Arabs who do not appear in the Bible, that the Quran affirms messengers to every nation, which explains shared beliefs across world religions, and that modern humans are equally arrogant about their permanence. Thamud were given clear guidance and preferred blindness. Only those with taqwa were saved, which he defines as preventive thinking about long-term harm. On the Day, the enemies of Allah are marched in ranks, refuse every outside witness, and are then testified against by their own hearing, sight and skins: their senses, which know they heard, saw and felt the truth. Everything is recorded within us, and they wrongly assumed Allah did not know much of what they did.

outline.heading: Recap: refusing to listen invites punishment
outline.gist: Dawah must be clear, rejecting the rational brings accountability, but character remains the best dawah.

outline.heading: Dawah happens on every level and has two sides
outline.gist: Parents, friends and children all try to influence one another; the speaker must be clear and the listener must listen.

outline.heading: Do as I do, not as I say
outline.gist: If what you preach has not inspired you to practise it, why should it inspire anyone else?

outline.heading: The Prophet spoke little and lived his message
outline.gist: His short, precise phrases could be memorised because people learned mostly from watching how he lived.

outline.heading: The listener's duty: actually listen
outline.gist: Many just wait for you to finish so they can repeat their line; you must process an argument before accepting or rejecting it.

outline.heading: A world where no one listens
outline.gist: Everyone pumps out their narrative; to be heard you must listen, as the Prophet did with Utbah.

outline.heading: Examples of those who did not listen
outline.gist: Utbah listened only partly; these verses show nations that did not listen at all.

outline.heading: 'Ad and the sites of punished nations
outline.gist: Their remains lie in Arabia; such places should be visited to take lessons, not as tourism.

outline.heading: Hud and Salih, prophets not in the Bible
outline.gist: Against the belief that prophets came only to the house of Abraham, the Quran says some messengers were named and others not.

outline.heading: A messenger to every nation
outline.gist: This explains why faiths across the world share ideas of reward, punishment, resurrection and revelation despite no contact.

outline.heading: Two lineages of Arabs
outline.gist: The ancient Arabs descended from 'Ad and Thamud's survivors and the Adnani Arabs from Ismail share a land and tongue but meet only at Nuh.

outline.heading: Muhajirun and Ansar under one roof
outline.gist: People came to Madinah amazed that the two lineages, who never mixed, now lived in the same homes.

outline.heading: Why the Quran tells the stories of Arab prophets
outline.gist: Earlier scriptures went to Bani Israel; the Quran addresses all, so its first hearers needed their own prophets' stories, and other peoples had theirs.

outline.heading: None like them in strength
outline.gist: Ancient structures suggest knowledge and precision we underestimate, yet whole civilisations were wiped out.

outline.heading: Who is mightier than us? Our arrogance too
outline.gist: Like 'Ad, we assume we are too significant to vanish; the One who created them is mightier.

outline.heading: A roaring wind in miserable days
outline.gist: Sarsar is a word formed from the sound of the wind itself.

outline.heading: Disgrace in this life, more in the next
outline.gist: Seven nights and eight days left them like hollow palm trunks; the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful still.

outline.heading: Thamud preferred blindness over guidance
outline.gist: They were given clearer guidance and still chose to remain blissfully ignorant, and the humiliating punishment took them.

outline.heading: Both nations simply refused to listen
outline.gist: Their prophets followed them everywhere; they demanded angels and would not give the message its time of day.

outline.heading: We saved those who believed and had taqwa
outline.gist: Wherever the Quran speaks of salvation or Paradise it mentions taqwa, which appears over 250 times.

outline.heading: Taqwa as prophylaxis
outline.gist: Taqwa is preventive thinking: asking before acting whether you will later regret it, and teaching the next generation to protect themselves.

outline.heading: The enemies of Allah marched in ranks
outline.gist: Being made to stand in orderly lines on the way to punishment is a deep humiliation.

outline.heading: Refusing every outside witness
outline.gist: Out of desperation they claim the earth, people and records are all lying and conspiring against them.

outline.heading: Hearing, sight and skins: the senses testify
outline.gist: Allah names the faculties, not the organs: the senses that heard, saw and felt the truth; skin symbolises feeling in the Quran.

outline.heading: Building a case against people we dislike
outline.gist: We hunt for flaws in what a disliked person says even when we know they are right, to protect our ego.

outline.heading: Why did you testify against us?
outline.gist: They address only their skins, the one tangible witness, thinking they were trying to protect them.

outline.heading: Allah made us speak the record
outline.gist: A witness can only testify to what happened; they heard, saw and felt it but denied what was there.

outline.heading: Everything is recorded inside you
outline.gist: Beyond the written book, our bodies already record what we witness; we are writing our own novel daily.

outline.heading: You did not see that one coming
outline.gist: They had a solid narrative rejecting external testimony but could not debunk an objective part of themselves.

outline.heading: You thought Allah did not know much of what you did
outline.gist: The verse's occasion: men at the Ka'bah debating whether Allah hears them if they speak quietly.

outline.heading: Outro

5021lTYJYro.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Ate and Dressed
5021lTYJYro.one_line: The Prophet's eating etiquette, diet and favourite foods, and the clothing he wore, as a picture of simplicity, gratitude and moderation.
5021lTYJYro.summary: He explains that learning small details about the Prophet builds a mental image of him that makes his example easier to follow. The Quran frames both topics: eat from what Allah provides and be grateful, wear your best to the masjid, and do not be wasteful. On eating, he covers saying bismillah, eating with the right hand from what is in front of you, eating together for blessing, and the Ash'ari tribe who pooled their food in hard times. The real lesson for today is to stop wasting food, especially in Ramadan. The Prophet never criticised food; he left what he disliked, such as lizard meat, without declaring it forbidden. He drank in three breaths, taught the one-third rule for the stomach, and sat in a way that respected food and limited how much he ate, staying fit into his sixties. He describes his favourite dishes, his rough barley bread, praising Allah after meals, and months of only dates and water. On dress, he preferred white, wore the qamis, turban, Yemeni striped cloaks and patched garments, held those closest to him to higher standards, and gave away a gifted garment that became a companion's shroud. The overall message is ease, moderation and gratitude.

outline.heading: Why details about him matter
outline.gist: The more details we know about the Prophet, the clearer the image of him in our minds, which helps us relate to and follow him.

outline.heading: Eat with gratitude; the garment of taqwa
outline.gist: Allah tells believers to eat from what He provided and thank Him, and reminds the children of Adam that He sent down clothing, and that the clothing of taqwa is best.

outline.heading: Adornment at the masjid, without waste
outline.gist: Wear your best clothing to the masjid and eat and drink without extravagance, for Allah does not love the wasteful.

outline.heading: Teaching a child to eat
outline.gist: He told a young companion making a mess to say Allah's name, eat with his right hand and eat from what is in front of him, and taught people to eat together for blessing.

outline.heading: The Ash'aris who pooled their food
outline.gist: In times of need a tribe would gather all their food and share it equally, and the Prophet said they are of him and he is of them.

outline.heading: The real lesson today: stop wasting food
outline.gist: With food so abundant, the key teaching is to avoid waste, especially in Ramadan, when cooking more and throwing it away contradicts the month and the Prophet's way.

outline.heading: He never criticised food
outline.gist: If he liked food he ate it, and if not he left it without a word. He was not fussy about details.

outline.heading: The lizard he would not eat
outline.gist: Offered roasted lizard, he did not eat it; asked if it was forbidden, he said no, it simply was not food of his people, and others ate it.

outline.heading: Drinking seated and in three breaths
outline.gist: He usually drank sitting but was also seen standing, showing the norm and the exception. He drank in three breaths.

outline.heading: A third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath
outline.gist: The worst vessel a person fills is his stomach; if he must eat more, a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breathing.

outline.heading: How he sat to eat, and never reclining
outline.gist: He sat on one leg with the other knee raised, which limits how much one eats, and never ate reclining out of respect for the blessing of food.

outline.heading: Fit to the end of his life
outline.gist: Into his sixties he stayed lean and fit without the belly that comes with age, the result of his eating habits.

outline.heading: His love of gourd
outline.gist: He loved a kind of squash cooked with dried meat; Anas would pick out the pieces for him and came to love it himself.

outline.heading: Honey sweets and tharid
outline.gist: He liked sweets with honey, and his most beloved dish was tharid, meat cooked with broken bread, sometimes with dried yogurt.

outline.heading: Milk, yogurt and meat
outline.gist: The many Arabic food names are confusing, but nearly all dishes were made from milk, yogurt and meat.

outline.heading: Watermelon with fresh dates
outline.gist: He ate a melon, probably watermelon, with fresh dates, one of his favourite pairings and what hosts tried to serve him.

outline.heading: Barley bread and a satisfied servant
outline.gist: He never ate refined white bread, only coarse unsifted barley bread. Allah is pleased with a servant who eats or drinks and then praises Him.

outline.heading: Praise after eating and the iftar dua for hosts
outline.gist: He praised Allah who fed and gave drink without our own power, and prayed for hosts that fasting people break their fast with them and the righteous eat their food.

outline.heading: The two black things: dates and water
outline.gist: Most of his diet was dates and water, and every meal included dates.

outline.heading: Months without a cooking fire
outline.gist: Two to three months could pass with no cooking in his house, yet he still enjoyed food when it came, such as meat and bread soup.

outline.heading: The rule: never seek, never refuse
outline.gist: He did not go out of his way for what was absent nor reject what was present. Flexibility, moderation, gratitude and rarely eating alone define his approach.

outline.heading: White clothing and the qamis
outline.gist: He said the best clothing is white, and his favourite garment was the qamis, with sleeves to the wrist and a button or two.

outline.heading: The turban as a symbol of scholarship
outline.gist: The turban began as Arab dress but became a mark of scholarship, which in many places one wears only when granted it by a scholar.

outline.heading: Turban colours and the Yemeni striped cloak
outline.gist: His teachers trace their turbans back through a chain to the Prophet's family. He wore white, green and black turbans, and liked striped Yemeni cloaks.

outline.heading: Silk lines and a higher standard for those close
outline.gist: Garments with some silk in them are acceptable for men. When he gave Ali a silk garment and Ali wore it, he was displeased: he held those closest to him to a higher standard.

outline.heading: Izar and rida
outline.gist: He wore unstitched upper and lower wraps, like the waist-cloth still worn in South Asia.

outline.heading: Yellowish and patched garments
outline.gist: He wore two-piece outfits, yellowish dyed clothes and patched garments; whatever was available.

outline.heading: The gifted garment that became a shroud
outline.gist: A woman made him a garment for the cold; a companion asked for it and was rebuked by others, but he wanted it as his shroud, and he died within the week and was buried in it.

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Such of you as put away your wives (by saying they are as their mothers) - They are not their mothers; none are their mothers except those who gave them birth - they indeed utter an ill word and a lie. And lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

58:3.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:3.en: Those who put away their wives (by saying they are as their mothers) and afterward would go back on that which they have said, (the penalty) in that case (is) the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. Unto this ye are exhorted; and Allah is Informed of what ye do

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who findeth not (the wherewithal), let him fast for two successive months before they touch one another; and for him who is unable to do so (the penance is) the feeding of sixty needy ones. This, that ye may put trust in Allah and His messenger. Such are the limits (imposed by Allah); and for disbelievers is a painful doom

eBAHzsddJrw.speaker: adnan
eBAHzsddJrw.speaker_note: single speaker teaching his Ramadan morning series on the Prophet's attributes
eBAHzsddJrw.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Treated Children and Women
eBAHzsddJrw.one_line: Stories of the Prophet's gentleness with children and his empowerment of women, ending with a case against barriers that exclude women in masajid.
eBAHzsddJrw.summary: Continuing his series on how the Prophet did things, he pairs two topics for scheduling reasons: children and women. With children he tells of visiting the dying Jewish boy who ran his errands, consoling little Abu Umayr when his pet bird died, taking along a young girl who followed the army and giving her a share of the spoils, and Anas serving nine years without once being scolded. He then counts the children who lived in the Prophet's house over his life, around nineteen plus grandchildren and young helpers, to show how much patience that required. On women he cites the woman who led him by the hand to see to her need, the hadith promising Jannah for raising daughters and sisters well, the girl who refused a forced marriage, the day set aside to teach women, Khawlah's argument that brought the verses on zihar, and Umm Hani's grant of protection being honoured. He warns that private advice the Prophet gave women should not be preached at them from the minbar. He closes by arguing that the Prophet's masjid had no barrier, that barriers alienate women, and that Muslims should simply behave professionally with each other as they do at work, because the ummah cannot move forward without women fully engaged.

outline.heading: Framing: how he treated children and women
outline.gist: Places the session within the series on how the Prophet did things and explains that the two topics are paired only for scheduling.

outline.heading: Visiting the dying Jewish boy who served him
outline.gist: A neighbour's young son ran errands for the Prophet; when he stopped coming, the Prophet asked after him and went to visit him at his deathbed.

outline.heading: Abu Umayr and the bird
outline.gist: He asked the little orphan boy about his bird every day, consoled him when it died, and played with children in the alleys.

outline.heading: The young girl on the campaign
outline.gist: He found a girl travelling with the army, kept her with him and gave her a necklace from the spoils like any participant.

outline.heading: Anas: nine years without a harsh word
outline.gist: Anas served him for nine years and was never asked why he did or did not do something, and was given playful nicknames.

outline.heading: Nineteen children in his household
outline.gist: He tallies his own children, stepchildren, cousins and young helpers who lived in his house, none of whom he ever hit or shouted at.

outline.heading: The woman who led him by the hand
outline.gist: A woman asked for his time and he walked with her wherever she needed until her matter was done, despite his burdens.

outline.heading: Jannah for raising daughters and sisters
outline.gist: Hadith promising Paradise and protection from the Fire to those who care for daughters or sisters and do not favour sons over them.

outline.heading: The girl who refused a forced marriage
outline.gist: A young woman whose father married her to his nephew came to the Prophet; she was given the choice and stayed, but wanted women to know they have that right.

outline.heading: A day set aside to teach women
outline.gist: He held a dedicated session where women learned and asked their questions.

outline.heading: Private advice to women is not minbar material
outline.gist: Some hadith addressed to wives were given in closed settings; they are advice women may take, not lines to be preached at them in public.

outline.heading: Khawlah and the verses on zihar
outline.gist: Zihar trapped women between marriage and divorce; Khawlah argued with the Prophet until revelation came, and he explains why both 'argue' and 'complain' are used in the verse.

outline.heading: Umm Hani's protection is honoured
outline.gist: When Ali pursued a fugitive she had sheltered, the Prophet upheld her grant of protection.

outline.heading: The women's pledge of allegiance
outline.gist: Women gave their own pledge like the men, without a handshake, and the wording of pledges varied with the person and context.

outline.heading: A leadership model that gave space and autonomy
outline.gist: Women and children were not afraid of him and felt free to come, argue, ask and complain, which was remarkable 1400 years ago.

outline.heading: Do not bar women from the masajid
outline.gist: Women are central to the deen, and the Prophet told men not to prevent women from coming to the masjid.

outline.heading: Barriers alienate
outline.gist: The Prophet's masjid had no curtain; any barrier between speaker and listener makes people feel excluded.

outline.heading: Behave as professionally as at work
outline.gist: Muslims deal with the other gender respectfully at work every day; doing the same in the masjid is harder than a barrier but is the sunnah.

outline.heading: The ummah needs women fully engaged
outline.gist: Regressing on what the Prophet opened up makes no sense; women must feel equal ownership of Islam for the community to move forward.
