25:27.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:27.en: On the day when the wrong-doer gnaweth his hands, he will say: Ah, would that I had chosen a way together with the messenger (of Allah)

25:28.ar: يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ لَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أَتَّخِذۡ فُلَانًا خَلِيلࣰ ا
25:28.en: Alas for me! Ah, would that I had never taken such an one for friend

25:29.ar: لَّقَدۡ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَنِيۗ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولࣰ ا
25:29.en: He verily led me astray from the Reminder after it had reached me. Satan was ever man's deserter in the hour of need

25:51.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَبَعَثۡنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرۡيَةࣲ نَّذِيرࣰ ا
25:51.en: If We willed, We could raise up a warner in every village

25:52.ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَجَٰهِدۡهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
25:52.en: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them herewith with a great endeavour

25:77.ar: قُلۡ مَا يَعۡبَؤُاْ بِكُمۡ رَبِّي لَوۡلَا دُعَآؤُكُمۡۖ فَقَدۡ كَذَّبۡتُمۡ فَسَوۡفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامَۢا
25:77.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): My Lord would not concern Himself with you but for your prayer. But now ye have denied (the Truth), therefor there will be judgment

26:52.ar: ۞وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَسۡرِ بِعِبَادِيٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
26:52.en: And We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night, for ye will be pursued

26:53.en: Then Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners

26:54.en: (Who said): Lo! these indeed are but a little troop

26:55.en: And lo! they are offenders against us

26:56.en: And lo! we are a ready host

26:57.en: Thus did We take them away from gardens and watersprings

26:58.en: And treasures and a fair estate

26:59.en: Thus (were those things taken from them) and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them

26:60.en: And they overtook them at sunrise

26:61.ar: فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ قَالَ أَصۡحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدۡرَكُونَ
26:61.en: And when the two hosts saw each other, those with Moses said: Lo! we are indeed caught

26:62.ar: قَالَ كَلَّآۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهۡدِينِ
26:62.en: He said: Nay, verily! for lo! my Lord is with me. He will guide me

26:63.ar: فَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرۡقࣲ كَٱلطَّوۡدِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
26:63.en: Then We inspired Moses, saying: Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast

26:64.en: Then brought We near the others to that place

26:65.en: And We saved Moses and those with him, every one

26:165.en: What! Of all creatures do ye come unto the males

26:166.ar: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمٌ عَادُونَ

26:167.ar: قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُخۡرَجِينَ

26:168.en: He said: I am in truth of those who hate your conduct

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

1kpTDle0LP4.speaker_note: leads the nightly reflections, refers listeners to his own surah-summary series and says he comes from Damascus
1kpTDle0LP4.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 18: Quranic Reflections (Al-Furqan to Al-Naml)
1kpTDle0LP4.one_line: Al-Furqan, al-Shu'ara and al-Naml: bad friends, striving with the Quran not the sword, dua as the reason Allah cares, Musa at the sea, and Lut's stance.
1kpTDle0LP4.summary: He closes his map of the cluster from al-Isra on carrying the message: al-Furqan lists what undermines it, al-Shu'ara deals with public narrative, al-Naml with power and status. He then takes selected passages. The wrongdoer biting his hands on Judgment Day regrets one bad friend; he ties that self-directed anger to self-harm, urges professional help, and tells the young that peer pressure works both ways, so choose ambitious, principled company and cut loose those who drag you down, as Uqbah's ruinous choice shows. The command to strive with the Quran, revealed in Makkah when fighting was forbidden, means striving with ideas and values; Islam was never spread by the sword, as surviving minorities in Damascus and the converted Mongols show, and anyone who needs force has no ideas. The last verse of al-Furqan says Allah would not care for us but for our dua, so he asks everyone to learn honest, personal supplication before the last ten nights. Musa at the sea answers by reflex that his Lord is with him: obey, leave outcomes to Allah, never question Him. Lut rejects his people's practice, not their attractions, and Muslims should neither join nor celebrate it.

outline.heading: Recap: the cluster on carrying the message
outline.gist: From al-Isra to al-Nur: responsibility, the four elements of a society, family, ease not misery, role models, the journey, investing in people, and teachings that protect a community.

outline.heading: Al-Furqan: a list of what undermines the message
outline.gist: Each paragraph of the surah names one negative influence on your capacity to carry the message: bad friends, lack of commitment, lack of ethics.

outline.heading: Al-Shu'ara: the public narrative
outline.gist: The surah retells stories from the outside, as the crowd heard them, and is named after the poets who were the media of their day.

outline.heading: Al-Naml: the role of power and status
outline.gist: Sulayman's strength made the difference, while the prophet in the next story could get nowhere without any standing.

outline.heading: Interlude
The wrongdoer who bites his hands over a friend
outline.gist: On Judgment Day a man regrets not taking the Prophet's path and blames one friend who pulled him away from a reminder he had already accepted.

outline.heading: Self-directed anger and self-harm
outline.gist: Biting oneself is anger at oneself; people who self-harm often are, without knowing it, and need a mental health professional to unpack why.

outline.heading: It was my friend: bad company at any age
outline.gist: Whether 15 or 85, a bad friend keeps pulling you off a clear path until it is too late.

outline.heading: Peer pressure works in both directions
outline.gist: Surround yourself with ambitious people of clear values and vision and they will pressure you upward, just as idle company pulls you down.

outline.heading: Be selfish about your friendships
outline.gist: You are not responsible for where your friends go, but you are for yourself; drop people who mock your goals and it will be the best choice you make.

outline.heading: Uqbah: persecutor who came close to Islam
outline.gist: The man behind the verses had abused the Prophet in Makkah, then softened and drew near to accepting Islam.

outline.heading: Uqbah's friend forces the wrong choice
outline.gist: His friend refused to speak to him unless he spat at the Prophet, and he chose the friend; one bad friend changed his whole ending.

outline.heading: Strive against them: not combat in a Makkan surah
outline.gist: Fighting was forbidden in Makkah, so jihad here cannot mean combat; combat is only one circumstantial form of striving.

outline.heading: What striving means
outline.gist: Striving is going after a goal knowing the obstacles in advance and being ready for them, unlike patience, which meets what you did not expect.

outline.heading: A great striving with the Quran
outline.gist: The pronoun refers to the Quran: the only great jihad named in the Book is with its values, arguments and teachings.

outline.heading: The sword never changed minds
outline.gist: Force makes people cling harder to their beliefs; neither the Prophet nor later conquests converted anyone by the sword.

outline.heading: Minorities who still live in the Muslim lands
outline.gist: Damascus holds tiny faith communities centuries old, and Christians and Jews have long lived unharmed across Middle Eastern cities.

outline.heading: The Mongols took the faith they came to destroy
outline.gist: They razed Baghdad yet melted into the Muslims and became Muslim, because the striving was with the Book.

outline.heading: Whoever needs a sword has no ideas
outline.gist: Good ideas need no force; the same holds for parents, teachers and rulers, who should reason rather than impose.

outline.heading: Al-Furqan ends with the people who overcome
outline.gist: After its warnings the surah describes the believers who can carry the message and gives them a last tool.

outline.heading: Why would your Lord care about you?
outline.gist: Humans are small and weak; the only reason Allah concerns Himself with us is that we call on Him.

outline.heading: Abandoning dua and its consequence
outline.gist: Addressed to Quraysh, the verse warns that refusing to call on Him brings a certain punishment; stop speaking to Allah and you are off the grid.

outline.heading: Learn to make dua as a servant
outline.gist: Before the last ten nights, learn to speak to Allah honestly, without a mask or formal script, as a servant to the Lord who owns him.

outline.heading: Refusing an open invitation
outline.gist: He offers to listen at any time while needing nothing from us; turning that down is a failure of manners, and dua is what keeps us in His care.

outline.heading: Musa trapped between the sea and Pharaoh
outline.gist: After nine rejected signs Musa leads his people out, Pharaoh pursues, and the sea blocks the only way he was told to go; his people did not know the ending.

outline.heading: My Lord is with me, He will guide me
outline.gist: Musa's reflex answer promised guidance, not survival, and he lined his people up to fight rather than despair.

outline.heading: The same answer as the Prophet in the cave
outline.gist: Both knew Allah was with them because they had done exactly what He commanded; prophets leave outcomes in His hands.

outline.heading: We will die anyway: be on the right side
outline.gist: Death is certain, only its timing varies, so what matters is following Allah's rules, not fear of the result.

outline.heading: Never doomed while with Allah
outline.gist: Even massacred, those who did right are not ruined; the sahaba carried this and we have lost it. Then the sea parts and Pharaoh drowns.

outline.heading: Do not question what Allah should have done
outline.gist: Replace that language with tasbih; questioning or accusing God is toxic and empties Islam of its essence.

outline.heading: Lut's people and the mates Allah created

outline.heading: Lut's answer: I reject what you do
outline.gist: He will not engage in, encourage or celebrate their practice; Muslims should take his words as their stance today.

outline.heading: A practice, not an identity
outline.gist: Islam sees it as a practice, not something innate; of countless ways to express sexuality only one is accepted, between husband and wife in marriage.

outline.heading: God and sexuality: one way only
outline.gist: All Abrahamic faiths and others agree; unlike food, where almost all is allowed, there is one God and one lawful expression of sexuality.

outline.heading: Islam judges expression, not attraction
outline.gist: Attraction is private and dealt with elsewhere; the Quran addresses behaviour, and Lut condemned the deed, never the attraction.

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

6c3ikkrPurA.title: Building Self-Discipline and Grit
6c3ikkrPurA.one_line: Ramadan reminders on day nine: renew intentions, quit smoking, and let fasting build self-discipline and grit that last beyond the month.
6c3ikkrPurA.summary: Delivered on the ninth day of Ramadan, this khutbah gives three reminders. First, renew your intentions: this is when attendance drops as people grant themselves excuses, yet as long as what you want from Allah keeps its value and has not been granted, there is no logic in easing off. He tells young people that life only gets busier, so now is the time to build a connection with Allah. Second, with permission he shares the story of a brother who quit smoking after a frightening lung lesion, and his son quit with him; he urges smokers to stop this month for their health, children and wealth. Third, the main point: Ramadan teaches self-discipline and grit. He cites the hadith that the strong person controls himself when provoked, and describes his own twenty-year habit of breaking the fast with only dates, water and soup, which changes why one fasts. Since people function on less food and sleep in Ramadan, extra blessings after it should produce more, not become barriers. In the second khutbah he reads Allah's lament that most nations did not keep their covenant: grit means staying the course, not being part-time Muslims. Ramadan proves you can; the question is whether you will.

outline.heading: Opening
Renew your intentions: they get rusty
outline.gist: Allah wants ease for you in fasting and wants you to complete the days (2:185). His Ramadan khutbahs are reminders, and the first is always the same: intentions get rusty and old, so install an internal reminder and use every Friday to renew them.

outline.heading: The day-nine dip
outline.gist: Near the end of the first third the numbers fall: guests, visits and tiredness become a free-day card, one day becomes three, and people reach the last ten nights barely able to manage them.

outline.heading: No logic in easing off
outline.gist: As long as what you want from Allah has not been granted and has not lost its value, there is no reason to reduce your effort; ask again why you want it and how much. Imams across the city report bigger crowds this year, so stay focused on the finish line.

outline.heading: To the young: now is the time
outline.gist: Whatever your age, life only gets busier after school, university, marriage and children; there is no later, better time to build your connection with Allah.

outline.heading: A lung lesion after 35 years of smoking
outline.gist: Shared with permission: a brother had a lesion that worried him and his physicians alike; it proved to be a severe infection, and after 35 years of smoking the sheikh suggested it might finally be time.

outline.heading: Father and son quit together
outline.gist: The brother quit completely, and so did his son; children of smokers smoke, and telling them not to while you do is hypocrisy. His home is now smoke-free and he has never felt better.

outline.heading: Stop smoking this Ramadan
outline.gist: There is no better time than a blessed day when you already go seventeen hours without smoking; quit for your health, your children and your wealth, and find baraka in your time and home.

outline.heading: Ramadan teaches grit and self-discipline
outline.gist: Third reminder, the bulk of the khutbah: after last week's compassion, Ramadan teaches grit and self-discipline. Without knowing the learning objective people go through the motions and reset afterward.

outline.heading: The strong person controls himself
outline.gist: The strong person is not the one who pins you to the pavement but the one who controls himself when his buttons are pushed. Carl Jung: enlightenment comes only through controlled strength and discipline.

outline.heading: Without discipline there is no height
outline.gist: No one achieves anything without discipline, as every parent of an undisciplined child knows; he introduces an exercise he has practised for twenty years: break the fast with a few dates, water and soup, nothing more.

outline.heading: The light iftar exercise
outline.gist: Students laugh at it every year until one tries it; a switch turns on when you realize you were fasting for the meal. With nothing to look forward to at Maghrib, the reason you fast changes, and the self fights hardest at the sight of hot food.

outline.heading: Levelling up: you are in control
outline.gist: Winning that fight is like levelling up in a game: you eat because you choose to, not because the self demands it, and you stop thinking about food altogether.

outline.heading: Fully functional on less
outline.gist: In Ramadan you work, pray and come to the masjid on far less food and sleep, so outside Ramadan, with more of both, your performance should be better.

outline.heading: Don't let Allah's extra blessings become barriers
outline.gist: If it is not, the extra food and sleep Allah gives are being used as obstacles between you and who you could be; be more productive after Ramadan, not less.

outline.heading: Interlude
Most nations could not keep a covenant
outline.gist: After the stories of the punished nations Allah says, almost in disappointment, that He found most of them not true to their covenant and quick to deviate (7:102); we too gave Him a covenant.

outline.heading: Grit means staying to the end
outline.gist: Grit is staying the course to the bitter end; those who work in masajid see people come and go constantly, and someone who stays from start to finish is a rare gem.

outline.heading: Ramadan proves you can
outline.gist: Life fluctuates in mood, health and time, but people with grit do not change with it; thirty days and nights of fasting and prayer show you can do it without being held back.

outline.heading: Not 'can you' but 'will you'
outline.gist: We are not part-time Muslims, here for Ramadan only. On the ninth day it is already established that you can; the question is whether you will, and on the Day of Judgment Allah will ask not whether you could but why you did not.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people have no better time than now; waiting for graduation, marriage or retirement is self-deception.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Smoking harms health, children who copy you, and wealth; quitting brings blessing to time, health and home.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Ramadan trains self-discipline: controlling yourself when provoked, breaking the fast lightly so the self obeys you, and using extra blessings to do more.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Grit is keeping your covenant with Allah to the end regardless of life's fluctuations; committed people are rare gems.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Allah will not ask whether you could but why you did not, since Ramadan proved your capacity.

11:112.ar: فَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَ وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطۡغَوۡاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
11:112.en: So tread thou the straight path as thou art commanded, and those who turn (unto Allah) with thee, and transgress not. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do

11:113.ar: وَلَا تَرۡكَنُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ فَتَمَسَّكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ
11:113.en: And incline not toward those who do wrong lest the Fire touch you, and ye have no protecting friends against Allah, and afterward ye would not be helped

11:116.ar: فَلَوۡلَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ أُوْلُواْ بَقِيَّةࣲ يَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡفَسَادِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّمَّنۡ أَنجَيۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡۗ وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَآ أُتۡرِفُواْ فِيهِ وَكَانُواْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
11:116.en: If only there had been among the generations before you men possessing a remnant (of good sense) to warn (their people) from corruption in the earth, as did a few of those whom We saved from them! The wrong-doers followed that by which they were made sapless, and were guilty

11:117.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ بِظُلۡمࣲ وَأَهۡلُهَا مُصۡلِحُونَ
11:117.en: In truth thy Lord destroyed not the townships tyrannously while their folk were doing right

12:4.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيۡتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوۡكَبࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ رَأَيۡتُهُمۡ لِي سَٰجِدِينَ
12:4.en: When Joseph said unto his father: O my father! Lo! I saw in a dream eleven planets and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating themselves unto me

12:5.ar: قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تَقۡصُصۡ رُءۡيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيۡدًاۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
12:5.en: He said: O my dear son! Tell not thy brethren of thy vision, lest they plot a plot against thee. Lo! Satan is for man an open foe

12:50.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱئۡتُونِي بِهِۦۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرۡجِعۡ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسۡـَٔلۡهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسۡوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِي قَطَّعۡنَ أَيۡدِيَهُنَّۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيۡدِهِنَّ عَلِيمࣱ‏
12:50.en: And the king said: Bring him unto me. And when the messenger came unto him, he (Joseph) said: Return unto thy lord and ask him what was the case of the women who cut their hands. Lo! my Lord knoweth their guile

12:77.ar: ۞قَالُوٓاْ إِن يَسۡرِقۡ فَقَدۡ سَرَقَ أَخࣱ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُۚ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفۡسِهِۦ وَلَمۡ يُبۡدِهَا لَهُمۡۚ قَالَ أَنتُمۡ شَرࣱّ مَّكَانࣰ اۖ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ
12:77.en: They said: If he stealeth, a brother of his stole before. But Joseph kept it secret in his soul and revealed it not unto them. He said (within himself): Ye are in worse case, and Allah knoweth best (the truth of) that which ye allege

12:80.ar: فَلَمَّا ٱسۡتَيۡـَٔسُواْ مِنۡهُ خَلَصُواْ نَجِيࣰّ اۖ قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمۡ قَدۡ أَخَذَ عَلَيۡكُم مَّوۡثِقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبۡلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمۡ فِي يُوسُفَۖ فَلَنۡ أَبۡرَحَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡذَنَ لِيٓ أَبِيٓ أَوۡ يَحۡكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِيۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
12:80.en: So, When they despaired of (moving) him, they conferred together apart. The eldest of them said: Know ye not how your father took an undertaking from you in Allah's name and how ye failed in the case of Joseph aforetime? Therefore I shall not go forth from the land until my father giveth leave or Allah judgeth for me. He is the Best of Judges

12:81.ar: ٱرۡجِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيكُمۡ فَقُولُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّ ٱبۡنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدۡنَآ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمۡنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلۡغَيۡبِ حَٰفِظِينَ
12:81.en: Return unto your father and say: O our father! Lo! thy son hath stolen. We testify only to that which we know; we are not guardians of the Unseen

12:82.ar: وَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنَّا فِيهَا وَٱلۡعِيرَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَقۡبَلۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
12:82.en: Ask the township where we were, and the caravan with which we travelled hither. Lo! we speak the truth

12:83.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلٌۖ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأۡتِيَنِي بِهِمۡ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
12:83.en: (And when they came unto their father and had spoken thus to him) he said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience! It may be that Allah will bring them all unto me. Lo! He, only He, is the Knower, the Wise

12:84.ar: وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبۡيَضَّتۡ عَيۡنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلۡحُزۡنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمࣱ‏
12:84.en: And he turned away from them and said: Alas, my grief for Joseph! And his eyes were whitened with the sorrow that he was suppressing

12:85.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ تَفۡتَؤُاْ تَذۡكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوۡ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَٰلِكِينَ
12:85.en: They said: By Allah, thou wilt never cease remembering Joseph till thy health is ruined or thou art of those who perish

12:86.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُواْ بَثِّي وَحُزۡنِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
12:86.en: He said: I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah, and I know from Allah that which ye know not

12:89.ar: قَالَ هَلۡ عَلِمۡتُم مَّا فَعَلۡتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذۡ أَنتُمۡ جَٰهِلُونَ
12:89.en: He said: Know ye what ye did unto Joseph and his brother in your ignorance

12:90.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُۖ قَالَ أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ وَهَٰذَآ أَخِيۖ قَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصۡبِرۡ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
12:90.en: They said: Is it indeed thou who art Joseph? He said: I am Joseph and this is my brother. Allah hath shown us favour. Lo! he who wardeth off (evil) and endureth (findeth favour); for lo! Allah loseth not the wages of the kindly

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful

HkvtFijMV60.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 12: Quranic Reflections (Hud and Yusuf)
HkvtFijMV60.one_line: Hud's three elements of reform and Yusuf's lessons: envy, guarding personal news, dignity and reputation, a parent's grief, complaining to Allah, and reconciling family.
HkvtFijMV60.summary: He closes Hud with the command to stand firm as commanded, the verse said to have greyed the Prophet's hair, and reads standing firm as incorruptibility. From it he draws three elements of reform: remove corruption, do not transgress by demonising society, and do not lean toward oppressors or lose one's identity. A community is spared collective punishment while reformers remain, but zealotry and assimilation both fail. Surah Yusuf, unique as one prophet's full story, teaches that envy can lead brothers to throw a child into a well and hide it for decades, so personal news, especially failure, should be shared only with those who truly love you. Imprisoned for years with a smeared name, Yusuf never bargained with his knowledge and refused release until his name was cleared, a lesson for anyone representing Islam on guarding reputation. Ya'qub's grief for Yusuf decades later shows how parents feel even when they never say it, and his complaint to Allah alone models how believers carry pain. Yusuf's composure and immediate forgiveness once his brothers admitted their wrong teach paying with one's ego to keep a family together, a model the Prophet followed at the conquest of Mecca.

outline.heading: Opening
Surah Yusuf: one prophet, one story
outline.gist: No other surah is wholly one prophet's story, and Yusuf's story is told nowhere else in the Quran, unlike Musa's.

outline.heading: The four indispensable parts, recapped
outline.gist: Remove the core of creed, reform, consistent ethics or the law of righteousness and the faith stops working.

outline.heading: How he groups the Quran into clusters
outline.gist: His division is one way of seeing the Quran, not the only one; it aligns each surah's verses in one direction so reflection becomes more productive.

outline.heading: Hud and its sisters made me grey
outline.gist: Asked about his few white hairs, the Prophet pointed to this verse: stand firm exactly as you were commanded.

outline.heading: Standing firm as incorruptibility
outline.gist: The straight path as commanded means no one can buy you, make you sell out or push you into shortcuts.

outline.heading: Reform begins by removing corruption
outline.gist: The first element of reform is identifying corruption in society, culture, tradition and practice and removing it.

outline.heading: Do not transgress: no demonising society
outline.gist: The second element: those obsessed with reform must not judge or look down on people who do not share their effort.

outline.heading: Do not lean toward the oppressors
outline.gist: The third element: never sell out or lose your identity to those in power, or the fire will touch you.

outline.heading: Reform is selfless, and Hud's story shows it
outline.gist: Reform offers the nafs little: no looking down on others and no deals with the powerful; every story in the surah carries all three elements.

outline.heading: A remnant forbidding corruption
outline.gist: If not for a small group in past nations who kept forbidding corruption, no one would have remained on earth.

outline.heading: No collective punishment while reformers remain
outline.gist: Punishment comes when people accept a corrupt reality and stop caring; walking the path of reform protects a community.

outline.heading: Two failures: zealotry and dissolving
outline.gist: Some grow so angry they kill their own brothers; others integrate until nothing of the deen is left; stay on the path between.

outline.heading: Yusuf's dream
outline.gist: The stars, sun and moon prostrating symbolise honouring his status; Ya'qub understood the boy had a remarkable future.

outline.heading: Do not tell your brothers
outline.gist: Ya'qub warned that the brothers would grow jealous and plot, but the child told them anyway, and jealousy is a lethal motive.

outline.heading: Guard your personal news
outline.gist: His teacher's advice: share successes only with those who love you and failures with those who truly love you; not everyone can handle your news.

outline.heading: Think of hasad as the brothers of Yusuf
outline.gist: Rather than imagining the evil eye as beams from someone's eyes, picture brothers throwing a six-year-old into a well.

outline.heading: Decades of hiding the crime
outline.gist: Envy can be strong enough that they never regretted it and kept the secret for about forty years until forced to admit it.

outline.heading: Your failures are when you are most vulnerable
outline.gist: Once shared, a secret is no longer a secret; be even more careful with failures, which others can use to push you down.

outline.heading: Choosing prison over the haram
outline.gist: A young slave whom no one would have judged, he refused repeatedly and asked for prison over sin.

outline.heading: Years in prison with a ruined reputation
outline.gist: He spent seven to nine years jailed under the very accusation he had refused, the kind of injustice that shakes weaker faith.

outline.heading: Interpreting the king's dream without bargaining
outline.gist: Untroubled by the injustice, he explained the seven good and seven hard years without asking for his release in return.

outline.heading: Knowledge is never a bargaining chip, and I will not leave
outline.gist: Sacred knowledge is shared when needed, never sold; when finally summoned he told the messenger to go back and have the women's case investigated.

outline.heading: Clear my name first: dignity
outline.gist: The Prophet humbly said he would have left at once; he meant to show Yusuf's composure in refusing freedom with a smeared name.

outline.heading: Guard your reputation if you represent Islam
outline.gist: People of taqwa leave anything that could harm their name; anyone representing Islam must not brush aside issues that can ruin their reputation.

outline.heading: Binyamin held and the eldest stays behind
outline.gist: Having sworn to bring all back, the eldest cannot face his father; the rest return and Ya'qub responds with beautiful patience.

outline.heading: Oh, my sorrow for Yusuf: how parents feel
outline.gist: He now calls this the most heartbreaking verse; after thirty-five years Ya'qub still grieves, and even a father who never praises you feels this way.

outline.heading: Eyes whitened with grief, and 'again with Yusuf'
outline.gist: He wept until he lost his sight, and his sons complained that he would destroy himself still talking about Yusuf.

outline.heading: Prophets feel pain but never object to Allah
outline.gist: Religious people feel the same sorrow as anyone; the difference is that they never turn to Allah in anger or blame Him.

outline.heading: Take your pain to the One who cares
outline.gist: People listen out of courtesy and have no time for your problems; Allah wants to hear you, so complain to Him.

outline.heading: Composure before the brothers who took his childhood
outline.gist: He lost his childhood, his land and years with a prophet father, the noble son of noble sons, yet did not tear them apart when they stood before him.

outline.heading: Bringing them to the point of apology
outline.gist: Instead of punishing them he kept Binyamin and made each visit harder, weakening them until they came humbled, asking for charity, and then asked what they had done with Yusuf.

outline.heading: They lied about him to his face
outline.gist: Earlier they had claimed Binyamin's brother also stole, slandering Yusuf in front of him, and still he held his composure.

outline.heading: Pay with your ego to keep the family together
outline.gist: He chose to bring his family together rather than jail his brothers; whatever price your ego pays is small next to his.

outline.heading: Forgiveness the moment they admitted it
outline.gist: The surah moves straight from their apology to his acceptance; he was ready to forgive, but nothing is fixed until the wrongdoer comes clean.

outline.heading: Your siblings are yours to care for
outline.gist: Shame on them for not getting there sooner, but that does not serve the family; your family is your responsibility, for better or worse.

outline.heading: No blame on you today: the Prophet's echo of Yusuf
outline.gist: At the conquest, a relative who had wronged the Prophet was told by a learned companion to repeat the brothers' words, and the Prophet answered at once as Yusuf did.

outline.heading: Outro

8:5.ar: كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَيۡتِكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لَكَٰرِهُونَ
8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:6.ar: يُجَٰدِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَقِّ بَعۡدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
8:6.en: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible

8:7.ar: وَإِذۡ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحۡدَى ٱلطَّآئِفَتَيۡنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمۡ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيۡرَ ذَاتِ ٱلشَّوۡكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعَ دَابِرَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
8:7.en: And when Allah promised you one of the two bands (of the enemy) that it should be yours, and ye longed that other than the armed one might be yours. And Allah willed that He should cause the Truth to triumph by His words, and cut the root of the disbelievers

8:8.ar: لِيُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَيُبۡطِلَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
8:8.en: That He might cause the Truth to triumph and bring vanity to naught, however much the guilty might oppose

8:41.ar: ۞وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمۡ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
8:41.en: And know that whatever ye take as spoils of war, lo! a fifth thereof is for Allah, and for the messenger and for the kinsman (who hath need) and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in Allah and that which We revealed unto Our slave on the Day of Discrimination, the day when the two armies met. And Allah is Able to do all things

8:17.ar: فَلَمۡ تَقۡتُلُوهُمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمۡۚ وَمَا رَمَيۡتَ إِذۡ رَمَيۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ وَلِيُبۡلِيَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡهُ بَلَآءً حَسَنًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
8:17.en: Ye (Muslims) slew them not, but Allah slew them. And thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw, that He might test the believers by a fair test from Him. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

9itA9GqAFYg.title: Building Adherence to Righteousness
9itA9GqAFYg.one_line: Mid-Ramadan khutbah: righteousness means doing the right thing, drawn from Badr, applied to Al-Aqsa, claiming rights and community outreach.
9itA9GqAFYg.summary: At the halfway mark of Ramadan he asks people to renew their intentions, notes the post-COVID rise in young people filling the masjids, and urges them to treat each of the last ten nights as possibly the last they will see, since Allah hides the Night of Decree just as He hides the hour of death and which deeds He accepts. His main point is that righteousness is simply doing the right thing, which is harder than it sounds because it means setting self-interest aside. Ramadan trains this by routine: more prayer, family meals, community and less consumption. He then retells the first Ramadan and Badr through the lens of Surah Al-Anfal: the companions thought the caravan was about money, but Allah frames it as standing for haqq. He links this to the Al-Aqsa raids, saying no one will care about Muslims' rights unless Muslims do. The verse 'you did not throw when you threw' teaches that people must give full effort while success comes from Allah. Today's forms of adherence are knowledge, community building and being a voice for others. He closes on outreach: the same 3,500 people fill every event while many times that number never come, so Muslims must welcome them back without judgment and move them even one step closer to righteousness, just as Al-Aqsa will change only when enough Muslims care.

outline.heading: Opening
Past the halfway line
outline.gist: The second half of Ramadan dominoes past far faster than the first, so this checkpoint is the time to renew your intentions and check you are on the way to what you hoped for.

outline.heading: Fuller masjids since COVID
outline.gist: Imams across the country have noticed people returning to the masjids in greater numbers and with more commitment since COVID, many of them young men and women eager to learn to worship; a sign the ummah is rising, not declining.

outline.heading: Allah hides everything
outline.gist: The moment of death, which dua and repentance He accepts, which sin brings punishment: all hidden, so people keep striving. The Night of Decree is hidden for the same reason, or people would come only that night.

outline.heading: Your last chance at the last ten nights
outline.gist: Tired and sleep-deprived, motivate yourself by imagining this is the last time you will ever witness the last ten nights; no one is guaranteed another.

outline.heading: Righteousness is just doing the right thing
outline.gist: Third reminder, the bulk of the khutbah: righteousness is a fancy word for doing the right thing in any situation, which is harder than it sounds.

outline.heading: Ramadan pushes you into doing right
outline.gist: Doing right means removing self-interest and taking the heavier route. Ramadan trains it by practice: more prayer and fasting, daily masjid, family meals, community, eating less and being healthier.

outline.heading: The first Ramadan
outline.gist: In the second year of Hijrah, 1442 lunar years ago, the companions first heard they would fast from sunrise to sunset under the desert sun and probably planned to sleep all day.

outline.heading: The caravan and the companions' objection
outline.gist: On the 17th of that first Ramadan the Prophet told them to go after the caravan carrying their stolen wealth; they argued that they had jobs and homes now, did not need the money, and need not poke the bear. The answer: who said this was about money?

outline.heading: Brought out for the truth
outline.gist: Your Lord brought you out for the truth while some believers disputed it as if being driven to their deaths (8:5-6): only 300 of them, barely armed, untrained.

outline.heading: Reminded every Ramadan of Al-Aqsa
outline.gist: Every Ramadan Muslims are made to watch the masjid dishonoured, still occupied by an apartheid state that respects neither human rights nor religious freedom and treats Muslims as less than human.

outline.heading: Claim your right back
outline.gist: You need not like that region or its people; a right taken unlawfully stays at the top of Muslim priorities until it is returned. Take back what was taken, and gift it afterward if you like, but it is your right.

outline.heading: Allah repeats the word haqq
outline.gist: The companions did not see at first that it was not about money, which is why Allah repeats the word haqq in these verses (8:7-8): the aim was to establish the truth.

outline.heading: Hard to unsee
outline.gist: Soldiers striking worshippers with rifle butts inside the house of Allah cannot be unseen, nor can the world acting as if it did not happen.

outline.heading: Why our blood seems cheap
outline.gist: Far smaller violations elsewhere make headlines while this goes unreported, leaving Muslims to ask whether they matter less; the lesson is not to expect anyone else to stand up for their rights.

outline.heading: The Day of Criterion
outline.gist: No one cares about your haqq but you, which is why the Prophet set out with two horses and 300 men, some very young; the Quran calls it the day that separated truth from falsehood (8:41).

outline.heading: Outnumbered three to one
outline.gist: No one would have bet on the Muslims against an army three times their size led by Quraysh, the protectors of the idols, yet despite their fear they stood their ground and saw it through.

outline.heading: Not a call to violence
outline.gist: What he asks for is true adherence to righteousness, the lesson Allah meant from Ramadan and from Badr.

outline.heading: Badr told through the lens of righteousness
outline.gist: A seerah lesson starts with the companions' debates and details; Allah tells the story through righteousness instead. That is why anyone present at Badr outranked every other companion.

outline.heading: You did not throw when you threw
outline.gist: You did not kill them, Allah did; you did not throw when you threw (8:17). You drew the bow and released the arrow, but it hit only by Allah's will; your part is to prove yourself and do the right thing.

outline.heading: Today's forms of adherence
outline.gist: The same question is asked of Muslims today without bows and arrows: through knowledge, community building, supporting people and being a voice for those without one, and caring about rights taken from Muslims worldwide.

outline.heading: The form changes, the concept doesn't
outline.gist: There is always a different way to stand by what is right; do your best for Allah and leave facilitation and success to Him. Muslims stress the second half of the sentence and neglect the first.

outline.heading: Where is the effort?
outline.gist: Success does not drop out of the sky; it comes through people exhausting their resources and taking a stand. Even when it fails, our job is to do what they did on the 17th of Ramadan.

outline.heading: Nothing outweighs righteousness
outline.gist: Put wealth, social standing, family or safety on one side of the scale and righteousness on the other, and everything else flies into the air: the lesson of Ramadan and of Badr.

outline.heading: Interlude
The same 3,500 people
outline.gist: Friends and relatives distant from Islam need to be heard. Around 3,500 people are recycled through every Jumuah, taraweeh, programme and dinner in the city, while eight or nine times as many Muslims live there.

outline.heading: From 50 meters to 49
outline.gist: Seven thousand appear at Eid and twelve thousand at a marketplace, yet there is no outreach welcoming them back with their struggles and sins. We are not here to judge; moving someone one step closer to Allah is worth it.

outline.heading: Al-Aqsa changes when enough Muslims care
outline.gist: Two billion voices cannot be ignored, but most are busy with games and travel, so a holy place where the prophets walked can keep being dishonoured. Serving distant Muslims is part of the same adherence to righteousness.

outline.heading: Interlude
The fatigue fades, the reward stays
outline.gist: Keep renewing your intention and commit for the few nights left; on Eid you will either have the reward or regret its absence, while the tiredness is forgotten after one long sleep.

outline.heading: Outro

16:96.ar: مَا عِندَكُمۡ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقࣲۗ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوٓاْ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:96.en: That which ye have wasteth away, and that which Allah hath remaineth. And verily We shall pay those who are steadfast a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do

17:13.ar: وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِي عُنُقِهِۦۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا يَلۡقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
17:13.en: And every man's augury have We fastened to his own neck, and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

17:22.ar: لَّا تَجۡعَلۡ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقۡعُدَ مَذۡمُومࣰ ا مَّخۡذُولࣰ ا
17:22.en: Set not up with Allah any other god (O man) lest thou sit down reproved, forsaken

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

17:24.ar: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
17:24.en: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little

17:59.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرۡسِلَ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّآ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلۡأَوَّلُونَۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبۡصِرَةࣰ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۚ وَمَا نُرۡسِلُ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّا تَخۡوِيفࣰ ا
17:59.en: Naught hindereth Us from sending portents save that the folk of old denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel - a clear portent save to warn

17:90.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
17:90.en: And they say: We will not put faith in thee till thou cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us

17:91.ar: أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةࣱ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَعِنَبࣲ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا
17:91.en: Or thou have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly

17:92.ar: أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
17:92.en: Or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us piecemeal, as thou hast pretended, or bring Allah and the angels as a warrant

17:93.ar: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتࣱ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبࣰ ا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا رَّسُولࣰ ا
17:93.en: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord be Glorified! Am I aught save a mortal messenger

17:105.ar: وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ نَزَلَۗ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
17:105.en: With truth have We sent it down, and with truth hath it descended. And We have sent thee as naught else save a bearer of good tidings and a warner

17:106.ar: وَقُرۡءَانࣰ ا فَرَقۡنَٰهُ لِتَقۡرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكۡثࣲ وَنَزَّلۡنَٰهُ تَنزِيلࣰ ا
17:106.en: And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

18:10.ar: إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةࣰ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:10.en: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight

18:11.ar: فَضَرَبۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ فِي ٱلۡكَهۡفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدࣰ ا
18:11.en: Then We sealed up their hearing in the Cave for a number of years

18:12.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰهُمۡ لِنَعۡلَمَ أَيُّ ٱلۡحِزۡبَيۡنِ أَحۡصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُوٓاْ أَمَدࣰ ا
18:12.en: And afterward We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties would best calculate the time that they had tarried

18:13.ar: نَّحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ نَبَأَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّهُمۡ فِتۡيَةٌ ءَامَنُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ وَزِدۡنَٰهُمۡ هُدࣰ ى
18:13.en: We narrate unto thee their story with truth. Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance

18:14.ar: وَرَبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ إِذۡ قَامُواْ فَقَالُواْ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَن نَّدۡعُوَاْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَٰهࣰ اۖ لَّقَدۡ قُلۡنَآ إِذࣰ ا شَطَطًا
18:14.en: And We made firm their hearts when they stood forth and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We cry unto no Allah beside Him, for then should we utter an enormity

18:15.ar: هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمُنَا ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةࣰۖ لَّوۡلَا يَأۡتُونَ عَلَيۡهِم بِسُلۡطَٰنِۭ بَيِّنࣲۖ فَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
18:15.en: These, our people, have chosen (other) gods beside Him though they bring no clear warrant (vouchsafed) to them. And who doth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie concerning Allah

18:16.ar: وَإِذِ ٱعۡتَزَلۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأۡوُۥٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ يَنشُرۡ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئۡ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَمۡرِكُم مِّرۡفَقࣰ ا
18:16.en: And when ye withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then seek refuge in the Cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a pillow in your plight

18:17.ar: ۞وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمۡسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهۡفِهِمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقۡرِضُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمۡ فِي فَجۡوَةࣲ مِّنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۗ مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ وَلِيࣰّ ا مُّرۡشِدࣰ ا
18:17.en: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it rose move away from their cave to the right, and when it set go past them on the left, and they were in the cleft thereof. That was (one) of the portents of Allah. He whom Allah guideth, he indeed is led aright, and he whom He sendeth astray, for him thou wilt not find a guiding friend

18:18.ar: وَتَحۡسَبُهُمۡ أَيۡقَاظࣰ ا وَهُمۡ رُقُودࣱۚ وَنُقَلِّبُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِۖ وَكَلۡبُهُم بَٰسِطࣱ ذِرَاعَيۡهِ بِٱلۡوَصِيدِۚ لَوِ ٱطَّلَعۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَوَلَّيۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ فِرَارࣰ ا وَلَمُلِئۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ رُعۡبࣰ ا
18:18.en: And thou wouldst have deemed them waking though they were asleep, and We caused them to turn over to the right and the left, and their dog stretching out his paws on the threshold. If thou hadst observed them closely thou hadst assuredly turned away from them in flight, and hadst been filled with awe of them

18:32.ar: ۞وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلࣰ ا رَّجُلَيۡنِ جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَحَفَفۡنَٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلࣲ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمَا زَرۡعࣰ ا
18:32.en: Coin for them a similitude: Two men, unto one of whom We had assigned two gardens of grapes, and We had surrounded both with date-palms and had put between them tillage

18:33.ar: كِلۡتَا ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ ءَاتَتۡ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمۡ تَظۡلِم مِّنۡهُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَفَجَّرۡنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرࣰ ا
18:33.en: Each of the gardens gave its fruit and withheld naught thereof. And We caused a river to gush forth therein

18:34.ar: وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرࣱ فَقَالَ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكۡثَرُ مِنكَ مَالࣰ ا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرࣰ ا
18:34.en: And he had fruit. And he said unto his comrade, when he spake with him: I am more than thee in wealth, and stronger in respect of men

18:35.ar: وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمࣱ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدࣰ ا
18:35.en: And he went into his garden, while he (thus) wronged himself. He said: I think not that all this will ever perish

18:36.ar: وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةࣰ وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَا مُنقَلَبࣰ ا
18:36.en: I think not that the Hour will ever come, and if indeed I am brought back unto my Lord I surely shall find better than this as a resort

18:37.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرۡتَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلࣰ ا
18:37.en: His comrade, when he (thus) spake with him, exclaimed: Disbelievest thou in Him Who created thee of dust, then of a drop (of seed), and then fashioned thee a man

18:38.ar: لَّٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:38.en: But He is Allah, my Lord, and I ascribe unto my Lord no partner

18:39.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالࣰ ا وَوَلَدࣰ ا
18:39.en: If only, when thou enteredst thy garden, thou hadst said: That which Allah willeth (will come to pass)! There is no strength save in Allah! Though thou seest me as less than thee in wealth and children

18:40.ar: فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَن يُؤۡتِيَنِ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡهَا حُسۡبَانࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصۡبِحَ صَعِيدࣰ ا زَلَقًا
18:40.en: Yet it may be that my Lord will give me better than thy garden, and will send on it a bolt from heaven, and some morning it will be a smooth hillside

18:41.ar: أَوۡ يُصۡبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوۡرࣰ ا فَلَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبࣰ ا
18:41.en: Or some morning the water thereof will be lost in the earth so that thou canst not make search for it

18:60.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَىٰهُ لَآ أَبۡرَحُ حَتَّىٰٓ أَبۡلُغَ مَجۡمَعَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ أَوۡ أَمۡضِيَ حُقُبࣰ ا
18:60.en: And when Moses said unto his servant: I will not give up until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, though I march on for ages

18:61.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجۡمَعَ بَيۡنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ سَرَبࣰ ا
18:61.en: And when they reached the point where the two met, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the waters, being free

18:62.ar: فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا قَالَ لِفَتَىٰهُ ءَاتِنَا غَدَآءَنَا لَقَدۡ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبࣰ ا
18:62.en: And when they had gone further, he said unto his servant: Bring us our breakfast. Verily we have found fatigue in this our journey

18:63.ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَ إِذۡ أَوَيۡنَآ إِلَى ٱلصَّخۡرَةِ فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ ٱلۡحُوتَ وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَنۡ أَذۡكُرَهُۥۚ وَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ عَجَبࣰ ا
18:63.en: He said: Didst thou see, when we took refuge on the rock, and I forgot the fish - and none but Satan caused me to forget to mention it - it took its way into the waters by a marvel

18:64.ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبۡغِۚ فَٱرۡتَدَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصࣰ ا
18:64.en: He said: This is that which we have been seeking. So they retraced their steps again

18:65.ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبۡدࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمۡنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلۡمࣰ ا
18:65.en: Then found they one of Our slaves, unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our presence

18:66.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلۡ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمۡتَ رُشۡدࣰ ا
18:66.en: Moses said unto him: May I follow thee, to the end that thou mayst teach me right conduct of that which thou hast been taught

18:67.ar: قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:67.en: He said: Lo! thou canst not bear with me

18:68.ar: وَكَيۡفَ تَصۡبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمۡ تُحِطۡ بِهِۦ خُبۡرࣰ ا
18:68.en: How canst thou bear with that whereof thou canst not compass any knowledge

18:69.ar: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرࣰ ا وَلَآ أَعۡصِي لَكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
18:69.en: He said: Allah willing, thou shalt find me patient and I shall not in aught gainsay thee

18:83.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِي ٱلۡقَرۡنَيۡنِۖ قُلۡ سَأَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۡهُ ذِكۡرًا
18:83.en: They will ask thee of Dhu'l-Qarneyn. Say: I shall recite unto you a remembrance of him

18:84.ar: إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ سَبَبࣰ ا
18:84.en: Lo! We made him strong in the land and gave him unto every thing a road

18:86.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغۡرِبَ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغۡرُبُ فِي عَيۡنٍ حَمِئَةࣲ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوۡمࣰ اۖ قُلۡنَا يَٰذَا ٱلۡقَرۡنَيۡنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمۡ حُسۡنࣰ ا
18:86.en: Till, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found a people thereabout. We said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Either punish or show them kindness

18:87.ar: قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوۡفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابࣰ ا نُّكۡرࣰ ا
18:87.en: He said: As for him who doeth wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with awful punishment

18:88.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۖ وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا يُسۡرࣰ ا
18:88.en: But as for him who believeth and doeth right, good will be his reward, and We shall speak unto him a mild command

18:90.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطۡلِعَ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطۡلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ لَّمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتۡرࣰ ا
18:90.en: Till, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had appointed no shelter therefrom

18:91.ar: كَذَٰلِكَۖ وَقَدۡ أَحَطۡنَا بِمَا لَدَيۡهِ خُبۡرࣰ ا
18:91.en: So (it was). And We knew all concerning him

T0__vc-T-oo.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 14: Quranic Reflections (An-Nahl and Al-Isra)
T0__vc-T-oo.one_line: From blessings to carrying the message: what a nation needs, the promise of a good life, the book each person writes, honouring parents, and the Quran as miracle.
T0__vc-T-oo.summary: He closes an-Nahl by stressing that blessings belong to Allah and must be used His way, then opens the largest cluster of the Quran, on carrying the message. Al-Isra hands the message to Muslims in the form of the Quran, and al-Kahf's four stories name what a nation needs: a solid idea, wealth, knowledge and power. Lacking all four, Muslims in Canada are a population rather than a nation, and he argues the only realistic step is a trusted central fund for zakat. The one promise Allah makes to individuals is a good life, meaning fulfilment and purpose, which people seek once basic needs are met and whose absence feeds anxiety and depression; everything else ends, so it is little. Each person is writing a book that Allah will publish and hand them to read, judging themselves, which is why no one in the fire will claim to be wronged. Excellence to parents is joined to tawhid itself: not even a sigh of objection, lowering the wing of humility, while parents should not wield this duty to control their children. Finally, the Prophet was given the Quran rather than physical miracles because a book of guidance lets people become the miracle.

outline.heading: Blessings are Allah's, to be used His way
outline.gist: An-Nahl, last of the blessings cluster, teaches that every blessing comes from Allah, so use it as its Owner wants, like using a host's belongings in his house.

outline.heading: Al-Isra: the beacon passes to Muslims
outline.gist: The largest cluster is about carrying the message; each generation from Nuh and Ibrahim carried it, and now Muslims hold sole responsibility for it in the form of the Quran.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf: idea, wealth, knowledge and power
outline.gist: The cave, the two gardens, Musa's journey for knowledge and the story of power name what a nation needs, which is why the surah is read every week.

outline.heading: A population, not a nation
outline.gist: Muslims here lack all four; centralising the religious idea is the hardest and, in his view, impossible.

outline.heading: Centralising education, politics or neighbourhoods
outline.gist: A coordinated plan for which professions to train, religion-based politics, or clustering like Chinatown or Little Italy are all out of reach.

outline.heading: A central Muslim fund
outline.gist: Ten or fifteen trusted people running one fund into which Muslims pay zakat could build schools, help people buy homes, marry and clear debts.

outline.heading: The only promise to the individual
outline.gist: Groups are promised much, but individuals are promised neither wealth, health nor victory; only a good life for whoever believes and does good, male or female.

outline.heading: A good life means meaning and fulfilment
outline.gist: Not the best car or house, but a life with significance and purpose, the thing humans seek most.

outline.heading: Meaning is sought once basic needs are met
outline.gist: Growing up where people could barely secure food, clothing and shelter, he learned late that fulfilment becomes the first search once needs are met; Allah owes us nothing else.

outline.heading: Emptiness behind anxiety and procrastination
outline.gist: A lack of fulfilment drives much anxiety, depression, low motivation and laziness; the believer has a reason to get up in the morning.

outline.heading: Whatever ends is little
outline.gist: What you have runs out and what is with Allah remains; anything that ends, however abundant, will seem small at the last moment.

outline.heading: Fulfilment is the one thing no one takes
outline.gist: Wealth and health are stripped away at the end, but the sense of fulfilment stays and goes with you to the next world.

outline.heading: Every person's destiny fastened to his neck
outline.gist: The word has several readings, all fitting; he takes it as destiny: your own choices decide what happens next.

outline.heading: We are all authors
outline.gist: Even those who hate reading are writing a novel until their last breath, yet few revise it or seek feedback on whether it is meaningful.

outline.heading: Allah publishes your book and hands it to you
outline.gist: No publisher needed: the book is delivered into your hand and you give a public reading, and the fewer listeners the luckier you are.

outline.heading: Judge yourself: read the story you wrote
outline.gist: The book opens when you could tell right from wrong and narrates your motives, intentions and consequences; imagine today what it will say.

outline.heading: No one in the fire claims oppression
outline.gist: After reading their own book people accept their destiny; they beg for mercy but none says they were wronged, unlike prisoners who all claim innocence.

outline.heading: The commandments begin with tawhid
outline.gist: These verses resemble the Ten Commandments Musa carried, opening with the central value of the ummah: serve none but Him.

outline.heading: Excellence to parents, joined to worship
outline.gist: The second command shares the first one's verse: give your parents the best you have, for they cared for you in years you cannot remember.

outline.heading: Not even one contraction
outline.gist: A man who carried his mother asked if he had repaid her and was told not even for one contraction of her labour.

outline.heading: Do not say even 'uff'
outline.gist: Feeling frustrated with ageing parents is normal payback, but never voice it, not even with a one-syllable word built on the weakest letter in Arabic.

outline.heading: Speak generously and lower the wing of humility
outline.gist: Do not correct or humiliate them publicly; lower the wing you would soar with so they can step on it.

outline.heading: Pray for them as they raised you
outline.gist: Ask Allah's mercy for them; this command alone is attached to His own, so worship Him and care for parents at the same time.

outline.heading: A nation that dishonours parents goes nowhere
outline.gist: Birr ranks third among the problems he deals with daily and needs unpacking, including parents' abuses of power.

outline.heading: Parents: apply birr to yourself, not your children
outline.gist: The Quran is for using on yourself; demanding birr from your children is self-serving, and you still owe it to your own parents.

outline.heading: Birr is meeting needs, not control
outline.gist: Children must support parents financially, socially and emotionally, but parents do not dictate what they study or where they work unless it is haram; overuse makes the card worthless.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet was not given physical miracles
outline.gist: Earlier nations were given signs like the parting sea and still disbelieved, so such signs were withheld.

outline.heading: Thamud's mocking demand and the she-camel
outline.gist: Half-drunk, they invented an absurd demand for a pregnant camel from a boulder; when it came they slaughtered it and its calf.

outline.heading: Gushing springs, gardens or a ladder to the sky
outline.gist: The Quraysh demanded wonders and a book brought down from heaven; the answer was: am I anything but a human messenger?

outline.heading: The Quran lets you become the miracle
outline.gist: A physical miracle works only for its witnesses and often not even them; a way of life lets a person transform through willpower and Allah's help.

outline.heading: Sent down in truth, recited slowly
outline.gist: It came as good news and warning, revealed in stages so that it would be understood and reflected on.

outline.heading: Ramadan clears distractions for the Book
outline.gist: Nothing in life matters as much as the Quran; Ramadan's nightly recitation is for reflecting and living it, and whoever falls in love with it always finds the way.

outline.heading: Outro

4:94.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا ضَرَبۡتُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلسَّلَٰمَ لَسۡتَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا تَبۡتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ كَثِيرَةࣱۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلُ فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا

EXpjy80-FhY.speaker: adnan
EXpjy80-FhY.speaker_note: single speaker continuing his Ramadan morning series on the Prophet's attributes
EXpjy80-FhY.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Treated Sinners and Non-Muslims
EXpjy80-FhY.one_line: Through a series of stories, the Prophet's tenderness toward sinners and non-Muslims: hating the sin, never the sinner, and always drawing people closer.
EXpjy80-FhY.summary: He asks how the Prophet dealt with people who rejected him and with Muslims who sinned, starting from the command to call with wisdom and good counsel and the reminder that believers were once in the same place. He then works through stories: the repeat drinker the Prophet defended because he loved Allah and His Messenger, Umar's gentle letter to a relapsed friend, Thumamah tied in the masjid and released until he chose Islam freely, the youth whose pledge was refused until he promised to stop harassing women, Safana and her brother Adi ibn Hatim, the young man who asked permission for zina and was reasoned with, the man who broke his Ramadan fast and went home with charity for his own family, Ali told that guiding one person outweighs all wealth, the letter that softened Khalid, and Ikrimah being invited back. His conclusion is that the Prophet never compromised on right and wrong yet never judged, humiliated or made enemies. He criticises Muslims who act as a morality police toward everyone and urges a minority community in the West to treat non-Muslims and struggling Muslims the way the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Framing: sinners and those who rejected him
outline.gist: Introduces the topic as something everyone should reflect on.

outline.heading: Call with wisdom; you were once like them
outline.gist: The command to invite with wisdom and the best manner, and the reminder that guidance was a favour granted to the believers, so be tender.

outline.heading: The repeat drinker who loved Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: When companions cursed a man punished for drinking, the Prophet forbade it and told them not to help Shaytan against their brother; he explains the man's nickname.

outline.heading: Umar's letter to a relapsed friend
outline.gist: Umar wrote to a friend who returned to drinking with the opening verses of Ghafir, reminding him without shaming him, and it brought him back.

outline.heading: Thumamah tied in the masjid and set free
outline.gist: The Prophet visited the captured chief daily, then released him without ransom; Thumamah, having watched the Muslims, accepted Islam.

outline.heading: No interest in starving people
outline.gist: When Thumamah cut off wheat to Makkah, the Prophet had the trade restored because food is not a weapon.

outline.heading: The youth who tugged a woman's garment
outline.gist: The Prophet withheld his hand at the pledge until the young man promised never to do it again, then accepted him.

outline.heading: Safana bint Hatim shown mercy
outline.gist: The captive daughter of Hatim al-Ta'i was freed, provided for and kept until a trusted escort could take her home.

outline.heading: Adi ibn Hatim and the three promises
outline.gist: The Prophet seated the fleeing chief on his own cushion, addressed each reason he hesitated, and promised safety, wealth and the fall of Persia, which Adi later witnessed.

outline.heading: Kindness to a non-Muslim mother
outline.gist: A companion was told to keep good ties with her mother who had not accepted Islam, with the verse allowing kindness to those who do not fight Muslims.

outline.heading: The young man who asked permission for zina
outline.gist: Instead of rebuking him, the Prophet asked if he would accept it for his mother, sister or daughter, then prayed for him, and the youth never thought of it again.

outline.heading: Visiting and gifting non-Muslim neighbours
outline.gist: He visited Jewish and pagan neighbours, gave them gifts and ate their food.

outline.heading: The man who broke his fast in Ramadan
outline.gist: Unable to do any expiation, he was given dates to give in charity and ended up feeding his own family; the Prophet read his context and never shamed him.

outline.heading: Ali at Khaybar: guiding one person
outline.gist: Before battle, Ali was told that Allah guiding one person through him is better than owning all the wealth on earth.

outline.heading: Kind words that won Khalid
outline.gist: A message praising Khalid's intellect and promising good treatment stayed with him until he accepted Islam.

outline.heading: Ikrimah invited back
outline.gist: Despite being sentenced, Ikrimah was sent for through his wife, turned back at the Red Sea, was welcomed, and the companions were told not to curse his father.

outline.heading: Hate the sin, not the sinner
outline.gist: He never compromised on what was wrong and still punished public sin, yet testified to the love of Allah in a drunkard.

outline.heading: Not the morality police
outline.gist: Some Muslims act as if at war with everyone; the prophetic way is to name the mistake and then help the person closer to Allah, and to leave peaceful non-Muslims their space.

outline.heading: A minority that follows his way
outline.gist: Living as a minority, Muslims should treat non-Muslims and struggling Muslims as he did, even when it is less satisfying for the ego.

themes.note: Pardon of enemies like Thumamah, Adi and Ikrimah, and gentleness with sinners.

41:23.ar: وَذَٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرۡدَىٰكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
41:23.en: That, your thought which ye did think about your Lord, hath ruined you; and ye find yourselves (this day) among the lost

41:24.ar: فَإِن يَصۡبِرُواْ فَٱلنَّارُ مَثۡوࣰ ى لَّهُمۡۖ وَإِن يَسۡتَعۡتِبُواْ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُعۡتَبِينَ
41:24.en: And though they are resigned, yet the Fire is still their home; and if they ask for favour, yet they are not of those unto whom favour can be shown

41:25.ar: ۞وَقَيَّضۡنَا لَهُمۡ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فِيٓ أُمَمࣲ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
41:25.en: And We assigned them comrades (in the world), who made their present and their past fairseeming unto them. And the Word concerning nations of the jinn and humankind who passed away before them hath effect for them. Lo! they were ever losers

41:26.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَا تَسۡمَعُواْ لِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَٱلۡغَوۡاْ فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَغۡلِبُونَ
41:26.en: Those who disbelieve say: Heed not this Qur'an, and drown the hearing of it; haply ye may conquer

41:27.ar: فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَسۡوَأَ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:27.en: But verily We shall cause those who disbelieve to taste an awful doom, and verily We shall requite them the worst of what they used to do

41:28.ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعۡدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُۖ لَهُمۡ فِيهَا دَارُ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يَجۡحَدُونَ
41:28.en: That is the reward of Allah's enemies: the Fire. Therein is their immortal home, payment forasmuch as they denied Our revelations

41:29.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيۡنِ أَضَلَّانَا مِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ نَجۡعَلۡهُمَا تَحۡتَ أَقۡدَامِنَا لِيَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَسۡفَلِينَ
41:29.en: And those who disbelieve will say: Our Lord! Show us those who beguiled us of the jinn and humankind. We will place them underneath our feet that they may be among the nethermost

41:20.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:20.en: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

41:22.ar: وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
41:22.en: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

39:10.ar: قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣱۗ وَأَرۡضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجۡرَهُم بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
39:10.en: Say: O My bondmen who believe! Observe your duty to your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint

70:4.ar: تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ‏
70:4.en: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years

73:2.en: Keep vigil the night long, save a little

73:3.en: A half thereof, or abate a little thereof

73:4.ar: أَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ تَرۡتِيلًا
73:4.en: Or add (a little) thereto - and chant the Qur'an in measure
