ImnJyMWrEJA.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 4 (41:23-29)
ImnJyMWrEJA.one_line: The false assumption that Allah does not know, choice as a closing window, companions who adorn bad deeds, and Quraysh drowning out the Quran.
ImnJyMWrEJA.summary: He restates that listening is obligatory and applies it to Muslims: we want others to judge Islam on its arguments rather than media reputation, so we owe other faiths the same fairness, and a faith built only on emotion and inheritance is fragile and can be toppled in a weak moment. Muslims should never fear an argument. Verse 23 names the root failure: assuming Allah does not know or care what we do. Verse 24 shows that patience and pleas for another chance, so rewarding in this life, mean nothing on the Day; free choice is a temporary window, and everyone will eventually turn to Allah, the only question being whether it counts. Verse 25 describes companions from jinn and humans who make bad deeds look good. He sees Shaytan as weak, like someone holding out a catalogue, whereas bad human friends are far more dangerous, since character spreads both ways. Choose your company carefully at every age, because time is your real capital. Verse 26 shows Quraysh telling people not to listen and to make noise, illustrated by Tufayl's cotton-stuffed ears, Nadr's fables and the Quraysh leaders secretly listening at night. He closes with recompense for the worst deeds and the unanswered plea to see those who misled them.

outline.heading: Recap: listening is obligatory
outline.gist: Rejecting something without hearing its argument and answering it with a stronger one is a cause for punishment.

outline.heading: Give others the fairness we ask for
outline.gist: We want people to judge Islam by its arguments, not media; we must not judge others by cultural reputation either.

outline.heading: The Prophet and the scholars knew other faiths
outline.gist: Muslims historically studied what other faiths say about themselves; his teachers were well versed in comparative religion.

outline.heading: Faith built on emotion and inheritance is fragile
outline.gist: Without having examined arguments, a Muslim is vulnerable when one appears at a moment of struggle.

outline.heading: Follow the truth wherever it is
outline.gist: A Muslim is not afraid: 'If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship'; this cluster gives seven pieces of advice on dawah.

outline.heading: Your senses are there to absorb
outline.gist: These pages stress listening; use your senses as you expect others to use theirs.

outline.heading: Recap: your own self used against you
outline.gist: The one thing they thought would protect them, their own body, becomes the record against them.

outline.heading: That assumption about your Lord ruined you
outline.gist: Assuming Allah did not see, did not care and kept no record was where they slipped, and it made them losers.

outline.heading: Patience on the Day changes nothing
outline.gist: Whether they endure or ask to be sent back, the Fire remains their abode.

outline.heading: In this life, patience and repentance pay hugely
outline.gist: The patient enter without reckoning, and the door of tawbah stays open until the soul reaches the throat or the sun rises from the west.

outline.heading: Free choice is a temporary window
outline.gist: A right that will be revoked is not truly a right; it is an opportunity to use before it closes.

outline.heading: Everyone will turn to Allah; the question is when
outline.gist: All will show patience, repent and make dua; only now does it carry reward.

outline.heading: Standing on the Day: two minutes to fifty thousand years
outline.gist: The length of standing varies with closeness to Allah; even a standing as long as one's life is spent turning to Him.

outline.heading: A horrible deal
outline.gist: Someone may spend longer than his lifetime in unaccepted worship, wishing the first seventy years could be ignored, but only those count.

outline.heading: You only live once, rightly understood
outline.gist: There are no second chances as in a video game; one shot means you must do it right.

outline.heading: Qurana': companions from humans and jinn
outline.gist: A qarin is always alongside you; Shaytan tries to taint any sincere act with a bad intention.

outline.heading: His view of the qarin
outline.gist: Scholars differ; he leans away from a single permanent jinn and sees it as Iblis assigning whispering.

outline.heading: Shaytan is just holding out a catalogue
outline.gist: His only power is showing hooks that catch the self's eye, as with stray thoughts in prayer; whims do the rest.

outline.heading: They adorned what was before and behind them
outline.gist: Tazyin makes something look beautiful when it is not, so past and present wrongs seem good.

outline.heading: Two definitions of loss, and the human companion is worse
outline.gist: Loss is a wrong assumption about Allah and following companions; a bad friend, unlike Shaytan, does not flee when you pick up the Quran.

outline.heading: Character works both ways
outline.gist: Good character carries dawah and bad character carries peer pressure; behaviour lands where words do not.

outline.heading: Saving someone who thinks wrong is right
outline.gist: When bad deeds are adorned, the only hope is that the adornment falls away so remorse becomes possible.

outline.heading: Bad friends at any age
outline.gist: Influence never stops; he has seen people in their seventies revert when meeting an old friend.

outline.heading: Time is your capital: choose your company
outline.gist: Be picky about who you spend time with, not about cars or clothes; a moment gone can never be bought back.

outline.heading: Do not listen to this Quran; make noise over it
outline.gist: Quraysh warned visitors that he would bewitch them with words, so people fled from hearing him.

outline.heading: Tufayl and the cotton in his ears
outline.gist: A learned poet stuffed his ears, then rebuked himself, listened and accepted Islam almost at once.

outline.heading: Why growth was slow until the treaty
outline.gist: Numbers trickled until the peace of Hudaybiyyah let people listen, then skyrocketed.

outline.heading: Drowning it out with fables
outline.gist: A man who had learned Persian and Roman tales told stories to rival the Prophet's so people would not hear.

outline.heading: Noise is the only thing holding Islam back
outline.gist: Propaganda keeps people from hearing a message that is simple, clear and brings serenity and purpose.

outline.heading: Quraysh leaders listening in the bushes at night
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan hid outside the Prophet's courtyard to hear his night recitation and bumped into two others.

outline.heading: Three nights and three broken oaths
outline.gist: They swore not to return but met again; masters of language, they had never heard anything like it.

outline.heading: Never be afraid of an argument
outline.gist: If you are confident in your creed, invite the best argument, but insist on also being heard.

outline.heading: Recompensed for the worst of their deeds
outline.gist: The disbelievers will taste severe punishment, repaid for the worst things they did.

outline.heading: Believers rewarded for their best moments
outline.gist: Allah rewards the believer for his best deeds as though they were all he did, so the joy is real.

outline.heading: An eternal abode for denying the signs
outline.gist: As with 'Ad, they saw and heard clearly but refused to observe and listen; the next verses on character are among the most recited.

outline.heading: Show us those who misled us
outline.gist: They ask to trample their misleaders from jinn and humans, and the plea is not even answered; prevent that feeling by choosing now.

outline.heading: Outro

41:30.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَبۡشِرُواْ بِٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُمۡ تُوعَدُونَ
41:30.en: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised

41:31.ar: نَحۡنُ أَوۡلِيَآؤُكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَا تَشۡتَهِيٓ أَنفُسُكُمۡ وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ
41:31.en: We are your protecting friends in the life of the world and in the Hereafter. There ye will have (all) that your souls desire, and there ye will have (all) for which ye pray

41:32.en: A gift of welcome from One Forgiving, Merciful

41:33.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
41:33.en: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

41:36.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
41:36.en: And if a whisper from the devil reach thee (O Muhammad) then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is the Hearer, the Knower

46:13.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
46:13.en: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and thereafter walk aright, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O Muhammad) a witness against these

Y7khFOto0AQ.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 5 (41:30-36)
Y7khFOto0AQ.one_line: Uprightness as incorruptibility, angels who calm the steadfast, good deeds as the best speech, and repelling evil with what is best.
Y7khFOto0AQ.summary: He explains why these verses are so loved: they deliver the surah's third point, that dawah through character is the most effective. Verse 30 joins belief in Allah with standing straight, which he defines as incorruptibility, being a straight shooter with no hidden agenda; this is what to look for in a spouse rather than counting prayers, and it is the true karamah. Young people should never drop this ideal. Angels descend on such people, removing fear of the future and grief over the present, which together breed anxiety, and they are allies in both worlds; Shaytan meanwhile strikes hardest at those closest to Allah, so no one has made it until inside Paradise. Verse 33 asks who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds and declares himself Muslim, deliberately counting deeds as speech because actions speak louder; the Prophet spoke little and is praised in the Quran as an example. Verse 34 commands repelling evil with what is best so an enemy becomes a close friend. The Prophet did this so completely that we forget the harm done to him, and the sheikh tells how a youth who mocked him became his student. This needs patience and a great share of character, letting go like releasing a curling stone, and seeking refuge from Shaytan's promptings.

outline.heading: Why these verses are so well known
outline.gist: Many have memorised or often heard them; he will show why they fit together and how they serve the surah's goal.

outline.gist: After clear articulation and the duty to listen, these verses make the case for dawah through character.

outline.gist: Echoed in Al-Ahqaf and in the Prophet's concise advice to say 'I believe in Allah' and then be upright.

outline.heading: A concept repeated seventeen times a day
outline.gist: We ask for the straight path in every rak'ah, so we cannot afford to misunderstand it; it is figurative, about how we live.

outline.heading: Not slipping around like a fox
outline.gist: Early authorities defined it as never taking shortcuts or back doors: a person of their word with no hidden agenda, a rare treasure.

outline.heading: What to ask about a suitor
outline.gist: Not how much he prays but whether he is on time, cares for his dependants, is kind in every mood and brings only halal home.

outline.heading: The true karamah
outline.gist: Material miracles are given to Muslims and non-Muslims; the real gift of the close is steadfast uprightness for life.

outline.heading: Keep this ideal as you grow older
outline.gist: Of all the idealism of youth that people drop, never drop the refusal to be corrupted.

outline.heading: Angels descend: do not fear, do not grieve
outline.gist: Identify the source of your ethics and commit to it; that is essentially all of Islam, and angels bring good news of Paradise.

outline.heading: Your allies, and all your souls desire and wish
outline.gist: Tashtahi is what the self craves and tadda'un what you merely conceive of; both will be granted.

outline.heading: Asking Allah until you are satisfied
outline.gist: In Paradise Allah lets His servant wish until done, then prompts more, then asks if he is pleased and grants His lasting pleasure.

outline.heading: Two nudges: the angel and Shaytan
outline.gist: Good thoughts are prompts from the angel and evil ones from Shaytan, who leaves a residue even when chained in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Prompts do not control you
outline.gist: These are only suggestions; the closer to Allah, the more positive prompts you receive.

outline.heading: The closer you are, the harder Shaytan strikes
outline.gist: Those near to Allah face a more severe blow because he finds them harder to reach.

outline.heading: 'Not yet': you have not made it until inside
outline.gist: A great imam on his deathbed told Shaytan 'not yet'; believing you have made it is the start of the slide.

outline.heading: Fear of the future and sadness of the present
outline.gist: Mixed together they produce anxiety and depression; the angels remove both.

outline.heading: Let the angels keep nudging you after Ramadan
outline.gist: Set yourself up so they continue pushing you toward good; Paradise is hospitality from the Forgiving, the Merciful.

outline.heading: Who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah?
outline.gist: The central verse of the passage: calling to Allah, doing righteous deeds and declaring 'I am of the Muslims'.

outline.heading: Why good deeds are counted as speech
outline.gist: Two of the three are things said, but the third is action, a deliberate puzzle in the wording.

outline.heading: Deeds speak louder
outline.gist: No one is better spoken than someone who does good deeds; actions last longer and carry further than talk.

outline.heading: The Prophet spoke little
outline.gist: He spoke only when needed, repeating short sentences three times, because his actions spoke for him.

outline.heading: No one is better spoken than you
outline.gist: Call to Allah, be the best person you can be, and do it under the banner of Islam, wherever Allah placed you.

outline.heading: When preaching is overrated we lose our way
outline.gist: If words were enough the Prophet would never have stopped talking; prophethood is explaining then practising.

outline.heading: Praised as an example, not an orator
outline.gist: The Quran praises him as a witness and gold standard; the companions were won by his compassion, humility, generosity and grit.

outline.heading: Under the umbrella of Islam
outline.gist: When people see good behaviour done as a Muslim, they become curious about what drives it.

outline.heading: Good and evil are not equal: repel with what is best
outline.gist: Answer evil not with more garbage but with something good and excellent.

outline.heading: Answering an insult with a blessing
outline.gist: When a man called the Prophet names, he replied with a prayer for him; everyone brings out what is inside them.

outline.heading: An enemy becomes an intimate friend
outline.gist: Wali hamim: someone who declared enmity turns into a close supporter.

outline.heading: Try it just once
outline.gist: Whether they gossiped, insulted or sabotaged you, respond once with the best you have and see what happens.

outline.heading: The more he is provoked, the more patient he becomes
outline.gist: The Torah's description of the final Prophet; this character is why so many people became Muslim.

outline.heading: He made us forget the harm done to him
outline.gist: He treated former persecutors so graciously that readers of the seerah forget what they did, whereas humans normally never forget harm.

outline.heading: Study what was done to him
outline.gist: Learn the background of how people treated him, then how he approached them later.

outline.heading: Swallow your ego and practise
outline.gist: Most people melt when garbage is returned as a rose; agreeing with the verse is pointless if no one practises it.

outline.heading: Everyone experiences evil; this never fails
outline.gist: Your hurt is not special; in his experience responding with good has never gone wrong, and the problem is always his own ego.

outline.heading: The young man on the tractor
outline.gist: As a teenage imam he was mocked daily by a youth who years later joined his Quran circle and confessed; he had known all along and chose good.

outline.heading: A force of good or a force of harm
outline.gist: People are generally good but weak and lost; he could have taken revenge but won a lifelong friend instead.

outline.heading: Only granted to those who are patient
outline.gist: Only those with real perseverance can respond this way; most are committed only part of the time.

outline.heading: A great portion of character
outline.gist: Hazz is an allotted share, here of character rather than words; it is hard because justice feels unserved.

outline.heading: Let it go like a curling stone
outline.gist: The moment the curler releases the stone is the image of letting go of hurt.

outline.heading: Holding on only harms you
outline.gist: The one who hurt you has forgotten; carrying it eats at you, so let go and show them your excellence.

outline.heading: Imagine being described like that
outline.gist: The verse twice names those who can do this: the patient and those with a great share.

outline.heading: When Shaytan pokes you, seek refuge
outline.gist: Nazgh is a tear or prod that plants a wrong thought; refuse to act on it and ask the All-Hearing, All-Knowing for protection.

outline.heading: The method of dawah in one sweep
outline.gist: Belief and uprightness, angels' support, deeds as speech, repelling evil with good, patience and refuge from Shaytan.

outline.heading: The most important dawah is to Muslims
outline.gist: Young and uncommitted Muslims will not watch a lecture but will notice your character and commit because of it.

outline.heading: Outro

14:7.ar: وَإِذۡ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمۡ لَئِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمۡۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدࣱ‏
14:7.en: And when your Lord proclaimed: If ye give thanks, I will give you more; but if ye are thankless, lo! My punishment is dire

14:35.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدَ ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱجۡنُبۡنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ ٱلۡأَصۡنَامَ
14:35.en: And when Abraham said: My Lord! Make safe this territory, and preserve me and my sons from serving idols

14:36.ar: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضۡلَلۡنَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيۖ وَمَنۡ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
14:36.en: My Lord! Lo! they have led many of mankind astray. But whoso followeth me, he verily is of me. And whoso disobeyeth me - Still Thou art Forgiving, Merciful

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

14:38.ar: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ تَعۡلَمُ مَا نُخۡفِي وَمَا نُعۡلِنُۗ وَمَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
14:38.en: Our Lord! Lo! Thou knowest that which we hide and that which we proclaim. Nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah

14:39.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى ٱلۡكِبَرِ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
14:39.en: Praise be to Allah Who hath given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac! Lo! my Lord is indeed the Hearer of Prayer

15:28.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَٰلِقُۢ بَشَرࣰ ا مِّن صَلۡصَٰلࣲ مِّنۡ حَمَإࣲ مَّسۡنُونࣲ‏
15:28.en: And (remember) when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am creating a mortal out of potter's clay of black mud altered

15:29.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
15:29.en: So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit, do ye fall down, prostrating yourselves unto him

15:30.en: So the angels fell prostrate, all of them together

15:31.ar: إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
15:31.en: Save Iblis. He refused to be among the prostrate

15:32.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا لَكَ أَلَّا تَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
15:32.en: He said: O Iblis! What aileth thee that thou art not among the prostrate

15:33.ar: قَالَ لَمۡ أَكُن لِّأَسۡجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقۡتَهُۥ مِن صَلۡصَٰلࣲ مِّنۡ حَمَإࣲ مَّسۡنُونࣲ‏
15:33.en: He said: I am not one to prostrate myself unto a mortal whom Thou hast created out of potter's clay of black mud altered

15:53.ar: قَالُواْ لَا تَوۡجَلۡ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمࣲ‏
15:53.en: They said: Be not afraid! Lo! we bring thee good tidings of a boy possessing wisdom

15:54.ar: قَالَ أَبَشَّرۡتُمُونِي عَلَىٰٓ أَن مَّسَّنِيَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ
15:54.en: He said: Bring ye me good tidings (of a son) when old age hath overtaken me? Of what then can ye bring good tidings

15:55.ar: قَالُواْ بَشَّرۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡقَٰنِطِينَ
15:55.en: They said: We bring thee good tidings in truth. So be not thou of the despairing

15:56.ar: قَالَ وَمَن يَقۡنَطُ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
15:56.en: He said: And who despaireth of the mercy of his Lord save those who are astray

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And wherein is beauty for you, when ye bring them home, and when ye take them out to pasture

16:51.ar: ۞وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ لَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِۖ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱ فَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱرۡهَبُونِ
16:51.en: Allah hath said: Choose not two gods. There is only One Allah. So of Me, Me only, be in awe

16:52.ar: وَلَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِبًاۚ أَفَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ
16:52.en: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth, and religion is His for ever. Will ye then fear any other than Allah

16:53.ar: وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعۡمَةࣲ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِۖ ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فَإِلَيۡهِ تَجۡـَٔرُونَ
16:53.en: And whatever of comfort ye enjoy, it is from Allah. Then, when misfortune reacheth you, unto Him ye cry for help

16:54.ar: ثُمَّ إِذَا كَشَفَ ٱلضُّرَّ عَنكُمۡ إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنكُم بِرَبِّهِمۡ يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:54.en: And afterward, when He hath rid you of the misfortune, behold! a set of you attribute partners to their Lord

2:126.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱرۡزُقۡ أَهۡلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَضۡطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
2:126.en: And when Abraham prayed: My Lord! Make this a region of security and bestow upon its people fruits, such of them as believe in Allah and the Last Day, He answered: As for him who disbelieveth, I shall leave him in contentment for a while, then I shall compel him to the doom of Fire - a hapless journey's end

pAsvWIaWU5g.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 13: Quranic Reflections (Ibrahim, Al-Hijr, An-Nahl)
pAsvWIaWU5g.one_line: Opening the cluster of Ibrahim, al-Hijr and an-Nahl on blessings: show gratitude, learn to see blessings as blessings, and know their only source is Allah.
pAsvWIaWU5g.summary: He opens a new cluster of three surahs devoted to the blessings Allah grants unasked. Ibrahim teaches gratitude, al-Hijr teaches the ability to recognise a blessing, and an-Nahl teaches that every blessing comes from Allah and must be used as He intends. In Ibrahim he explains that kufr there means refusing to acknowledge a favour, and that the harshest consequence is losing blessings without noticing, such as the sweetness of calling on Allah. Ibrahim's closing prayer shows a prophet's vision of a safe land and a heart that asks forgiveness even for those who disobey him. From al-Hijr he argues that Iblis looked down on the very clay that made Adam unique, just as people fail to see their hardships or their own restless nafs as gifts, and even Ibrahim briefly doubted the news of a son. From an-Nahl he dwells on the beauty Allah placed in creation, illustrated by colourblind people seeing colour for the first time, and defines entitlement as fixating on what one lacks. He asks people to thank Allah for what they already have before asking for more, and to remember that good reaching them through others still comes from Allah.

outline.heading: A cluster of three surahs on blessings
outline.gist: Ibrahim on gratitude, al-Hijr on the ability to recognise blessings, an-Nahl on Allah as their single source and using them as He intends.

outline.heading: If you are grateful I will increase you
outline.gist: A standing law for all of history; kufr in this surah means refusing to acknowledge a favour, not disbelief, and reading it that way makes the whole surah cohere.

outline.heading: The severe punishment: blessings taken without notice
outline.gist: The worst loss is not noticing what was removed, as in the symbolic tale of a man who sinned for forty years and lost the sweetness of calling on Allah.

outline.heading: Honour blessings before they leave a home
outline.gist: A narration of weak chain, widely used by scholars, telling Aisha to treat Allah's blessings well because once they leave a household they rarely return.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's personal prayer and his vision of a safe land
outline.gist: Allah discloses Ibrahim's private prayer, including thanks for sons in old age; his utopia was safety, where people live and believe without fear for their lives.

outline.heading: Whoever follows me is of me: the heart of a prophet
outline.gist: Followers become his family through the bond of tawhid, stronger than blood, and for those who disobey he still asks Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

outline.heading: Hardships recognised as blessings only later
outline.gist: It takes time to see that a difficult childhood or struggle made us who we are; other blessings we never see at all.

outline.heading: Iblis scorns the altered clay of Adam
outline.gist: Proud of being made from fire, Iblis judged Adam by his nature, seeing only dried clay with rotting mud inside.

outline.heading: The rotting mud was the source of Adam's uniqueness
outline.gist: Life comes from water and soil left to ferment; the human is this earthy mix joined with the spirit from Allah, and Iblis missed the blessing in it.

outline.heading: Harnessing the nafs instead of letting it rot
outline.gist: Jealousy, lust and greed carry enormous energy; channelled into love and selflessness they make a person unstoppable.

outline.heading: The Prophet's relentless energy and Abu Sufyan
outline.gist: After twenty years of hostility Abu Sufyan, forgiven, wept at how patient the Prophet was; he won with ethics, kindness and love.

outline.heading: Ibrahim, the news of a son and not despairing
outline.gist: Even Ibrahim briefly met glad tidings negatively in old age, then corrected himself; from that son came the line of the Israelite prophets.

outline.heading: Livestock and the blessing of beauty
outline.gist: An-Nahl counts blessings one after another; amid warmth, food and transport it pauses on the beauty of animals at rest and at pasture.

outline.heading: Colourblind people seeing colour: hearts made for beauty
outline.gist: Ugliness comes from within, not from creation; the tears of people seeing colour for the first time show the heart is designed to absorb beauty.

outline.heading: One God to revere, to whom all religion belongs
outline.gist: Do not seek two gods; every faith traces back to Him and He alone deserves reverence and mindfulness.

outline.heading: Every blessing is from Allah: the trap of entitlement
outline.gist: Entitlement is fixating on the few things you lack; thank Allah for the blessings you have before demanding the next one.

outline.heading: Turning to Allah only in hardship, and blessings attributed elsewhere
outline.gist: People ignore blessings until difficulty, then forget again once relieved; in context, associating others means crediting a blessing to its channel instead of its source.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Gratitude is owed before anything else; ingratitude is refusing to acknowledge a favour and is punished by losing blessings unnoticed.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim's prayer reveals a vision of a safe society and a prophet's heart that wants guidance and forgiveness even for those who refuse him.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Hardships often prove to be the greatest blessings, though we only see it in hindsight.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Failing to see a blessing as a blessing: Iblis with Adam's clay, and even Ibrahim with the news of a son.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The nafs has rot in it but immense power; harnessed into love and selflessness it becomes unstoppable, as the Prophet showed.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Only the misguided despair of Allah's mercy; Ibrahim corrected himself and was given a lineage of prophets.

themes.label: Beauty in creation and appreciating it
themes.note: Allah made creation beautiful for us to absorb and reflect on; we take colour and beauty for granted until we see someone receive it.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Entitlement fixates on what is missing and unsettles faith; acknowledge what you have before asking for more.

quran.point: The other occurrence of Ibrahim's prayer for a safe land

hadith.gist: The Prophet saw food on the floor and told Aisha to honour Allah's blessings, since blessings that leave a household rarely return; he notes its chain is weak but scholars widely cite it.
The Prophet foretold a day when a woman could travel alone from Iraq to the Kaaba and back fearing no one.

maxims: You have to see blessings as blessings
Kufr is refusing to acknowledge good done to you
Entitlement is focusing on what you don't have
The ugliness in the world comes from within
Show gratitude before you ask for more

stories.who: A man who sinned for forty years (symbolic tale from the old tazkiyah books)
stories.point: He felt unpunished but had lost the sweetness of calling on Allah without noticing.

stories.who: Iblis and Adam
stories.point: Iblis despised the earthy, fermenting clay that was in fact the source of Adam's life and greatness.

stories.who: Abu Sufyan before the Prophet
stories.point: Forgiven after years of hostility, he marvelled at the Prophet's patience; ethics and love won where war did not.

stories.who: Ibrahim receiving news of a son in old age
stories.point: Even the best can fail to see a blessing for a moment; from that son came generations of prophets.

takeaways: Thank Allah for the blessings you already have before asking for the next one.
Look back at past hardships and recognise what good they produced in you.
Channel the strong drives of the nafs into love, selflessness and service.
Pause to absorb the beauty in creation instead of taking it for granted.
Remember that good reaching you through people comes from Allah, and thank Him for it.

25:63.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنࣰ ا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ ا
25:63.en: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace

FvzqrAMswk4.speaker: adnan
FvzqrAMswk4.speaker_note: continues his Attributes of the Prophet series, recapping his previous episodes
FvzqrAMswk4.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Spoke and Walked
FvzqrAMswk4.one_line: How the Prophet spoke, concise, clear, gentle and adapted to his listeners, and how he walked, turned, sat, rode and lay down.
FvzqrAMswk4.summary: He notes that no one in history has been described as thoroughly as the Prophet, and that the Quran itself teaches how to speak and how to walk. On speech: say good or stay silent, and faith is not upright until the heart is, which needs the tongue to be upright first. The Prophet never used obscenity, backbit or shouted; his harshest rebuke was a mild phrase. He spoke so sparingly his words could be counted, clearly and purposefully, repeating key points three times so listeners could memorise them, which is why so much of his teaching survives. He was soft and smiling in conversation yet transformed on the pulpit, warning of an army at the gates. He spoke to tribes in their own dialect, and even in grief at his son Ibrahim's death said only what pleases Allah. On movement: he walked briskly as if descending a slope, humbly, sometimes barefoot, never with people walking behind him for show, and turned his whole body to whoever addressed him to give full attention. He rode and sat in many ways and slept on his right side. He closes with the gift of saying much in few words.

outline.heading: Opening
The Quran teaches how to speak and walk
outline.gist: No one was described in such detail as the Prophet. The Quran describes the servants of the Merciful walking humbly, and he taught to say good or keep quiet.

outline.heading: An upright tongue makes an upright heart
outline.gist: Faith is not upright until the heart is, and the heart not until the tongue is. He never spoke obscenely, never backbit and never raised his voice.

outline.heading: His harshest rebuke
outline.gist: When he wanted to rebuke or tease someone, the strongest he would say was a mild phrase, 'may your forehead be in the dust'.

outline.heading: Few, clear words you could count
outline.gist: He spoke so little that one could count his words, distinctly and only as much as was needed, so that a listener could memorise it. Otherwise nothing would have been preserved.

outline.heading: Repeating three times; dignity in silence
outline.gist: He repeated important words three times so everyone heard and felt addressed. He was revered when silent and radiant when he spoke, passionate about his message.

outline.heading: Smiling, neither too much nor too little
outline.gist: He always smiled while explaining, spoke just enough for clarity, and never dragged on until listeners grew bored.

outline.heading: Soft-spoken, until he rose to the pulpit
outline.gist: His speech was gentle and tender, but on the minbar his face reddened and his voice rose as if warning of an enemy army arriving by morning.

outline.heading: Speaking in his listeners' dialect
outline.gist: Visitors who replaced 'al' with 'am' asked about fasting while travelling, and he answered them in their own dialect, knowing the accents of the Arabs.

outline.heading: Only words that please Allah, even in grief
outline.gist: Sobbing at his son Ibrahim's death, he explained that tears are not disobedience and that they would say only what pleases their Lord.

outline.heading: How he walked
outline.gist: He walked briskly with strength, as if going downhill, yet humbly. He did not want people walking behind him, leaving his back to the angels, and sometimes went barefoot.

outline.heading: Turning his whole body to the listener
outline.gist: When a stone injured his toe he said it is only a bleeding toe spent for Allah. He turned with his whole torso rather than just his neck, to give a person his full attention.

outline.heading: How he rode and sat
outline.gist: He rode horses, camels, mules and donkeys, saddled or not, and sat in many postures: squatting on his feet, cross-legged, one leg over the other, reclining, on the bare ground or on a mat.

outline.heading: How he lay down, and why it was recorded
outline.gist: The companions watched and described every daily movement. He usually lay on his right side with his hand under his head, sometimes using his sandals as a pillow.

outline.heading: Saying much in few words
outline.gist: His speech was concise, clear and fluent without ambiguity; five of his words can take days to explain. He knew the dialect of every people and spoke to them in a way they understood.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: Detailed description of the Prophet's speech and bodily manners.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Say good or be silent; an upright tongue makes an upright heart; no obscenity, backbiting or shouting.

themes.label: Public speaking and khutbah delivery
themes.note: Concise, clear, repeated, adapted to the audience, and intense on the minbar.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: He walked humbly and refused to have people walk behind him.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Turning fully toward whoever spoke to him, and his everyday manners in sitting, riding and sleeping.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Grief expressed through tears but only words that please Allah.

quran.point: The servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth in humility.

hadith.gist: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say good or remain silent.
A person's faith is not upright until his heart is upright, and his heart is not upright until his tongue is.
His strongest rebuke was to say: what is wrong with him, may his forehead be in the dust.
Aisha: if someone wanted to count his words, he could have counted them.
He would repeat a word three times so it would be understood.
When he gave a sermon his eyes reddened and his voice rose as if warning of an army.
He answered a tribe in their dialect that fasting while travelling is not part of righteousness.
At Ibrahim's death: the eye weeps, the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord.
When his toe was injured: you are but a toe that bled, and it was in the path of Allah.

maxims: Five words from him can take five days to explain

stories.who: Death of Ibrahim, the Prophet's son
stories.point: Grief and tears are not disobedience as long as speech stays pleasing to Allah.

takeaways: Speak less, more clearly and only as much as is needed.
Repeat key points so listeners retain them.
Address people in language they understand.
Turn your whole attention, even your body, to whoever is speaking to you.
Avoid obscenity, backbiting and raising your voice.

10:57.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم مَّوۡعِظَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَشِفَآءࣱ لِّمَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ وَهُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣱ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
10:57.en: O mankind! There hath come unto you an exhortation from your Lord, a balm for that which is in the breasts, a guidance and a mercy for believers

10:88.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ ءَاتَيۡتَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَأَهُۥ زِينَةࣰ وَأَمۡوَٰلࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَۖ رَبَّنَا ٱطۡمِسۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَٱشۡدُدۡ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ
10:88.en: And Moses said: Our Lord! Lo! Thou hast given Pharaoh and his chiefs splendour and riches in the life of the world, Our Lord! that they may lead men astray from Thy way. Our Lord! Destroy their riches and harden their hearts so that they believe not till they see the painful doom

10:89.ar: قَالَ قَدۡ أُجِيبَت دَّعۡوَتُكُمَا فَٱسۡتَقِيمَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعَآنِّ سَبِيلَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
10:89.en: He said: Your prayer is heard. Do ye twain keep to the straight path, and follow not the road of those who have no knowledge

10:90.ar: ۞وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغۡيࣰ ا وَعَدۡوًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَكَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَتۡ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓاْ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
10:90.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his hosts pursued them in rebellion and transgression, till, when the (fate of) drowning overtook him, he exclaimed: I believe that there is no Allah save Him in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who surrender (unto Him)

10:91.ar: ءَآلۡـَٰٔنَ وَقَدۡ عَصَيۡتَ قَبۡلُ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
10:91.en: What! Now! When hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the wrong-doers

10:92.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنۡ خَلۡفَكَ ءَايَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ
10:92.en: But this day We save thee in thy body that thou mayst be a portent for those after thee. Lo! most of mankind are heedless of Our portents

10:98.ar: فَلَوۡلَا كَانَتۡ قَرۡيَةٌ ءَامَنَتۡ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَٰنُهَآ إِلَّا قَوۡمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّآ ءَامَنُواْ كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡيِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَتَّعۡنَٰهُمۡ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
10:98.en: If only there had been a community (of all those that were destroyed of old) that believed and profited by its belief as did the folk of Jonah! When they believed We drew off from them the torment of disgrace in the life of the world and gave them comfort for a while

11:29.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
11:29.en: And O my people! I ask of you no wealth therefor. My reward is the concern only of Allah, and I am not going to thrust away those who believe - Lo! they have to meet their Lord! - but I see you a folk that are ignorant

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

11:44.ar: وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِي مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِي وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَٱسۡتَوَتۡ عَلَى ٱلۡجُودِيِّۖ وَقِيلَ بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:44.en: And it was said: O earth! Swallow thy water and, O sky! be cleared of clouds! And the water was made to subside. And the commandment was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon (the mount) Al-Judi and it was said: A far removal for wrongdoing folk

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Lo! my son is of my household! Surely Thy promise is the truth and Thou are the Most Just of Judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said: O Noah! Lo! he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct, so ask not of Me that whereof thou hast no knowledge. I admonish thee lest thou be among the ignorant

11:87.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
11:87.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! Doth thy way of prayer command thee that we should forsake that which our fathers (used to) worship, or that we (should leave off) doing what we will with our own property. Lo! thou art the mild, the guide to right behaviour

11:88.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَرَزَقَنِي مِنۡهُ رِزۡقًا حَسَنࣰ اۚ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُخَالِفَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنۡهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُۚ إِنۡ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِصۡلَٰحَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُۚ وَمَا تَوۡفِيقِيٓ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُ وَإِلَيۡهِ أُنِيبُ
11:88.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you: if I am (acting) on a clear proof from my Lord and He sustaineth me with fair sustenance from Him (how can I concede aught to you)? I desire not to do behind your backs that which I ask you not to do. I desire naught save reform so far as I am able. My welfare is only in Allah. In Him I trust and unto Him I turn (repentant)

QuGtMQHfyJI.speaker: adnan
QuGtMQHfyJI.speaker_note: leads the nightly reflections and refers to the surah summaries he gave over the previous four years
QuGtMQHfyJI.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 11: Quranic Reflections (Yunus and Hud)
QuGtMQHfyJI.one_line: Yunus and Hud: the Quran as cure, Musa's prayer against Pharaoh, accepting Allah's decree, independent scholars, Nuh's son, and Shu'ayb's motto of reform.
QuGtMQHfyJI.summary: He introduces the four surahs after the long seven, each guarding an indispensable part of Islam: Yunus on a core of creed, Hud on the message as reform, Yusuf on consistent ethics and ar-Ra'd on the law of always standing by right. The Quran is a reminder, cure, guidance and mercy, but it cures only those who admit their hearts are ill and come seeking the right thing. Musa's prayer that Pharaoh's circle not be guided is unique in the Quran, permitted only against extreme tyranny. Pharaoh's belief at drowning was rejected while Yunus's people were spared, and we do not know why; accepting Allah's decree means not demanding reasons and never ruling on others' faith. The prophets' refusal of payment leads him to the independence of scholars: Ahmad, Malik and Abu Hanifa would not be owned, and imams whose livelihood depends on boards lose their voice, so future imams need their own professions. Nuh's son, lost beneath a wave, is the most heartbreaking passage; he urges people not to judge struggling parents and not to let children grow up isolated. Shu'ayb's words, wanting only reform as far as he can, are the Muslim's motto.

outline.heading: After the long seven: four surahs on indispensable parts
outline.gist: The long seven tell the full story of faith; the next four, each about a hundred verses, take parts without which religion stops working, like essential parts of a car.

outline.heading: Four disciplines, and Yunus on creed
outline.gist: Creed, message, ethics and law; Yunus treats a part of belief without which faith eventually crashes, however much one believes in Allah.

outline.heading: Hud: a message without reform is ritual
outline.gist: If Islam does not come to a society pointing out mistakes and fixing them, it becomes a set of cultural rituals.

outline.heading: Yusuf and ar-Ra'd: consistent ethics and standing by right
outline.gist: Generosity only when rich is not an ethic, so consistency makes ethics real; ar-Ra'd sets the non-negotiable law of supporting what is right whether or not it suits you.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder, cure, guidance and mercy
outline.gist: The Quran reminds, cures the diseases in the chest such as arrogance, envy, indifference and lust, guides and shows compassion.

outline.heading: No cure without acknowledging the illness
outline.gist: As elderly patients who deny hypertension and diabetes cannot be treated, a Muslim who does not admit the nafs is sick gets nothing from the Quran.

outline.heading: What does connecting even mean?
outline.gist: People complain they do not connect with the Quran without defining what they seek; name the disease you feel and look for its cure.

outline.heading: Ask the pharmacy for the right thing
outline.gist: Come to the Quran feeling misguided and distracted, seeking redirection, cure, guidance and mercy, as you would ask for the right medicine.

outline.heading: Musa's prayer against Pharaoh's wealth
outline.gist: After years of dawah and nine signs, with his people still enslaved and dying, Musa asked Allah to remove the blessing from the wealth they used to misguide and oppress.

outline.heading: The one prophetic prayer that they not be guided
outline.gist: Prophets sometimes prayed for punishment but never against guidance; this is the only such prayer in the Quran.

outline.heading: A permission only against the worst tyranny
outline.gist: It allows the gravely oppressed to pray this way against a tyrant who enslaved a people for centuries; otherwise we always pray for people's guidance.

outline.heading: Pharaoh believes as he drowns
outline.gist: Pursuing the Israelites to kill them, he declared belief in the God of the Children of Israel and submission as the sea closed over him.

outline.heading: Too late: his body preserved as a sign
outline.gist: After a life of corruption his last-moment belief was rejected and his corpse kept as a lesson for those after him.

outline.heading: Why Pharaoh rejected but Yunus's people spared?
outline.gist: Yunus's people were forgiven despite a decreed punishment; explanations are guesses, and it is fine not to know why Allah accepts one and not another.

outline.heading: Accepting the decree, and not our call to judge
outline.gist: Part of the deen is accepting what Allah decrees and moving on; as with Usama, no human may reject someone's declaration of faith, only Allah may.

outline.heading: I ask you for no wealth
outline.gist: The prophets repeatedly told their people they wanted no payment; knowledge of Allah's word is beyond any transaction.

outline.heading: Paid scholars lose their autonomy
outline.gist: Teachers may be paid, but once a scholar is owned by whoever controls his money he cannot speak his mind and corruption begins in small steps.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad gleaning wheat for a living
outline.gist: Without another craft he gathered grain left after harvest rather than live off his knowledge.

outline.heading: Imam Malik and the caliph
outline.gist: He accepted gifts but made the caliph sit on the ground like everyone else, refusing to be bought.

outline.heading: Abu Hanifa, unowned in life and death
outline.gist: He opposed tyranny until he died in prison and willed not to be buried in a cemetery partly built on stolen land; give your wealth to institutions, not to buy scholars.

outline.heading: Imams who must read the paper they are handed
outline.gist: Across the ummah, imams dependent on their posts read what they are given; if communities pay imams, they must protect their freedom from boards and donors.

outline.heading: Imam Ahmad's ordeal was about autonomy
outline.gist: The created-Quran question was an obscure philosophical debate; he endured years of prison because the ruler had no right to dictate what a scholar says.

outline.heading: Raise imams with their own professions
outline.gist: Future imams should be doctors, engineers, lawyers or craftsmen who fund their own work; the Prophet never asked for anything and his descendants may not take charity.

outline.heading: Nuh sees his son among the waves
outline.gist: The most heartbreaking passage: after centuries of dawah, a father on the deck of an ark built on a mountain spots his unbelieving son as the flood rises.

outline.heading: Ride with us; I will seek a mountain
outline.gist: Nuh pleads with his son to believe now; the son trusts his swimming and a mountain, and Nuh warns that nothing protects from Allah's command but His mercy.

outline.heading: The wave between them, and Nuh at the intercession
outline.gist: It was the last time he saw his son; on the Day of Judgment, as each prophet declines to intercede, Nuh's reservation is what he asked after this.

outline.heading: He is not of your family
outline.gist: Nuh reminded Allah of His promise to save his family; the answer was that his family are the believers who stood by him, not a son who turned away.

outline.heading: Do not judge parents who struggle with their children
outline.gist: Blood means little without faith, but no one is better than Nuh; help a straying child find the way back or hold your tongue.

outline.heading: He was apart: do not isolate your children
outline.gist: The son was in a place apart; do not let children grow up distant from you, push them away or let them push you away.

outline.heading: Your child wants you
outline.gist: A child is ready to be your best friend; if the relationship fails it is on the parent, and Muslim minorities in the West cannot afford children isolated from family and masjid.

outline.heading: Does your prayer tell us what to do with our wealth?
outline.gist: Shu'ayb's people wanted a benign religion of rituals that changes nothing, mocking him sarcastically as the wise and forbearing one.

outline.heading: I will not do what I forbid you
outline.gist: He holds himself to the standard he preaches.

outline.heading: I only want reform as far as I am able
outline.gist: Correct and fix what you can, with success only from Allah and constant repentance; he asks people to read it daily as the Muslim's motto.

outline.heading: Outro
